title: Autonomous Cyber Operations Gym for Training and Evaluating AI Models for Defence
abstract: This paper proposes an Autonomous Cyber Operations (ACO) gym, a unified framework integrating high-fidelity network emulation, realistic user behaviour modelling for benign network traffic and adversarial profiles, and the generation of cybersecurity scenarios through open toolkits. By supporting live and deferred feature extraction at the packet and flow levels, the gym facilitates the creation of labelled synthetic datasets for training Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs), as well as developing and evaluating modular components for autonomous defence agents through emulated interactions. While evaluation of a DNN classifier within the gym shows high in-domain performance, achieving near-perfect recall on adversarial network flows, our experiments reveal a significant sensitivity to domain shift, showing that even minor changes in network composition, such as variations in traffic protocol distribution, can lead to a catastrophic collapse in model transferability and detection performance.

title: Multimodal Contrastive Representation Learning Based Voice Conversion for Electrolaryngeal Speech Enhancement
abstract: Electrolaryngeal (EL) speech suffers from severe acoustic mismatches with normal speech, resulting in degraded naturalness and intelligibility. These mismatches also make sequence-to-sequence voice conversion struggle to learn robust intermediate representations, hindering EL-speech-to-normal-speech conversion (EL2SP) performance. To address this, we propose a novel multimodal contrastive representation learning framework to 1) achieve richer multimodal-representation learning, and 2) facilitate the transferability of multimodal representations to speech-only EL2SP. First, EL speech and text representations are fused to learn multimodal representations for target speech generation, during which cross-modal contrastive learning is employed to encourage a semantically consistent speech--text representation space. Next, the fused representations are treated as a fixed target to guide speech-only representation learning through cross-stage contrastive learning, enabling multimodal knowledge to be transferred to the EL2SP task while preserving architectural and inference simplicity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms both the speech-only and multimodal-based baselines.

title: Workflow implementations in applications with MCP and large language models
abstract: V zaključnem delu je obravnavana implementacija delovnih tokov v aplikacijah s pomočjo protokola Model Context Protocol (MCP) in velikih jezikovnih modelov. Razvit je bil prototip proizvodnega sistema, ki naravni jezik prevaja v operacije prek 35 orodij MCP. Na 175 testih sta bila primerjana oblačni model OpenAI in lokalni model Ollama glede točnosti, hitrosti, kakovosti in zvestobe odgovorov. Ugotovljeno je bilo, da lokalni model doseže primerljivo točnost pri rutinskih ukazih in enakovredno kakovost odgovora, a je približno šestnajstkrat počasnejši ter manj zanesljiv pri zahtevnih ukazih z več argumenti.

title: Biomimetic Phononic Channels for Room-Temperature Quantum Coherence: Non-Markovian Vibronic Coupling, Thermal-Fluctuation Harvesting, and Generalized Adaptive Phonon-Gates in Solid-State Qubit Architectures
abstract: Description / Abstract: A central dogma of modern quantum information science asserts that macroscopic quantum superposition in solid-state devices requires millikelvin cryogenic environments ($T \approx 10\text{--}15\,\text{mK}$) to freeze out thermal phononic decoherence. Conversely, natural biological complexes---such as the Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) photosynthetic light-harvesting complex and avian cryptochrome magnetoreceptors---sustain functional electronic and spin quantum coherences at physiological temperatures ($T \approx 300\,\text{K}$). Biology resolves the thermal paradox not by suppressing environmental thermal fluctuations, but by employing structured, non-Markovian vibronic protein environments that actively harvest ambient heat to dynamically repump coherent phase trajectories. This treatise establishes the theoretical foundation and solid-state engineering architecture for Biomimetic Phononic Channels (BPCs) that replicate biological coherence mechanisms in artificial solid-state qubit platforms: (1) We formulate a non-Markovian open quantum Hamiltonian wherein engineered acoustic modes couple resonantly to electronic spin and transmon transitions, creating an underdamped vibronic shield with structured Lorentzian spectral densities; (2) We demonstrate the Environment-Assisted Quantum Transport (ENAQT) harvesting mechanism, proving that tuned non-Markovian phonon modes convert broadband thermal noise into constructive phase-locking drivers, attenuating the pure dephasing rate $\Gamma_\phi \to 0$ even as $k_B T \gg \hbar \omega_{\text{qubit}}$; and (3) We generalize our foundational Adaptive Phonon-Gate into the Generalized Adaptive Phonon-Gate (GAPG), utilizing piezoelectric lithium niobate ($\text{LiNbO}_3$) and diamond acoustic metamaterial superlattices to vent destructive incoherent high-frequency phonons while confining constructive vibronic modes. We present rigorous master equations, finite-element phononic bandgap dispersions, and benchmarking projections establishing a direct pathway toward room-temperature fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Developing salesperson AI wisdom along the B2B customer buying journey
abstract: AI in B2B sales is evolving beyond descriptive analytics toward prescriptive and generative tools that recommend, or even produce, a course of action. These outputs reach the salesperson looking like finished decisions, even though they often embed the priorities of whoever configured the tool, arrive too fast to examine, and remain invisible to the buyer. Foundational selling competencies were not built for this judgment. We introduce salesperson AI wisdom (SAIW), grounded in Sternberg’s Balance Theory of Wisdom, defined as the salesperson’s capability, developed through experience, to determine whether to follow, adapt, or override AI-generated outputs in ways that balance salesperson interests, buyer buying-job needs, and vendor organization objectives in pursuit of the common good. Anchored in the buyer’s journey, our framework maps SAIW across three stakeholder groups and six buying jobs from Jobs-to-Be-Done theory, positioning it as a moderator of how AI outputs translate into buyer-advancing actions. SAIW surfaces misalignment between the seller’s pipeline stage and the buyer’s current job that seller-centric models miss, distinguishes two wisdom enactment modes, and advances nine propositions on how it develops, moderates this translation, and is shaped by deployment mode, journey complexity, and vendor’s internal team actions.

title: A scoping review of transformer and large language model approaches for word sense disambiguation in multilingual and low resource settings from 2019 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Background In natural language processing, word sense disambiguation (WSD) is still a significant difficulty, especially in low-resource, multilingual environments with few annotated resources. Contextual semantic representation and WSD performance have been enhanced by recent developments in transformer architectures and large language models (LLMs). However, there is still little evidence synthesis in multilingual and genuine low-resource situations, and research is still dispersed across architectures, datasets, and evaluation systems. Methods In order to map evidence on transformer and LLM-based Word Sense Disambiguation techniques published between 2019 and January 2026, this scoping study used the PRISMA-ScR methodology. Google Scholar database was searched for relevant literatures. Studies that used transformer or LLM-based techniques for WSD and reported evaluation criteria like accuracy or F1-score were considered eligible. A structured framework comprising model architectures, datasets, evaluation techniques, adaption strategies, and important discoveries was used to chart the data descriptively. Results Nine studies were included in the analysis. Gloss-aware transformers, poly-encoder architectures, multilingual transfer learning, morphologically aware fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adapters, and LLM-based reasoning were among the main topics. Model scale alone does not seem to have as much of an impact on WSD performance as architectural design and contextual modeling. Evidence for really low-resource languages was still scarce, though. Conclusion Transformer and LLM-based methods show immense potential for improving WSD in multilingual contexts. However, there are still gaps in robustness assessment, benchmark standardization, and the wider inclusion of low-resource languages that are underrepresented.

title: Open-set encrypted traffic recognition via contrastively-optimized multi-modal gating and extreme value theory
abstract: The widespread adoption of cryptographic protocols has rendered traditional payload inspection ineffective, necessitating advanced encrypted traffic analysis. Identifying unseen zero-day threats within encrypted streams, defined as the open-set problem, remains challenging due to adversarial feature manipulation, metric distortion induced by traditional cross-entropy optimization, and the resulting overconfidence of closed-set classifiers. In this paper, we propose Contrastively-Optimized Multi-Modal Gating with Extreme Value Theory (COMG-EVT), an open-set encrypted traffic recognition framework designed to establish strict rejection boundaries for unknown attacks. The framework integrates three core mechanisms: a dynamic GatedFusion module that leverages stable microscopic payload entropy to modulate vulnerable macroscopic topological graphs, mitigating shortcut learning against obfuscation; a two-stage graph contrastive optimization paradigm that improves representation consistency and class-aware latent-space organization to reduce metric distortion; and a calibrated multi-gate EVT engine that models extreme tail distributions to mathematically bound the open space. We conduct extensive experiments on two contemporary datasets, including the cipher-agnostic CipherSpectrum dataset. The analytical results demonstrate that COMG-EVT outperforms state-of-the-art open-set methodologies, effectively minimizing the false positive rate for zero-day attacks while maintaining high classification accuracy for known traffic categories, thereby exhibiting robust resilience against dynamic open-space risks. Not applicable.

title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
abstract: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.

title: Fairness under Prediction Error in Predict-then-Optimize Pipelines
abstract: Fairness constraints in predict-then-optimize pipelines are necessarily enforced on predicted outcomes $\hat{y}$, since true outcomes $y$ are unobserved at decision time. We study whether a demographic parity constraint enforced this way continues to hold against $y$, and how the resulting violation scales with prediction error. Using a budget-constrained allocation problem solved as a linear program, we show empirically that the true-outcome fairness gap grows with prediction error $σ$ and saturates, well fit by $c(1 - e^{-σ/τ})$ with $c = 0.1545 \pm 0.0103$ and $τ= 3.9045 \pm 0.3745$; its mean is invariant to sample size while its variance decays at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ rate. We derive a two-part theoretical bound: a closed-form local sensitivity result showing the gap's first-order response to prediction error depends on only two individuals per group, validated against the solver to within three significant figures; and a universal, error-independent ceiling following from the boundedness of the decision variable, confirmed consistent with but looser than the empirical saturation level. On US Census income data, enforcing demographic parity on a trained predictor's output reduces an unconstrained disparity in true income to roughly one-third of its original size, leaving 34.4% $\pm$ 3.3% (California) and 35.7% $\pm$ 1.8% (Texas) of the disparity intact and undetectable from the predictions alone -- consistent not only in mechanism but in approximate magnitude across two states with different demographics and income distributions, and stable across ten independent train/test splits in each. A fairness constraint that appears fully satisfied at decision time can mask a substantial, systematic violation of the outcome it was meant to protect.

title: FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval
abstract: Evaluating fashion retrieval systems remains challenging due to the limited availability of benchmarks that capture the fine-grained, open-ended queries encountered in real-world search and recommendation. Existing benchmarks often rely on manual curation, predefined taxonomies, or synthetic prompts, limiting scalability and semantic coverage. We introduce FASHION-RQ: Mining Hierarchical Semantic Structure for Automated Evaluation of Fashion Retrieval, an automated framework that derives user-type queries and relevance sets directly from catalog structure. Our key insight is that hierarchical discrete representations learned by Residual Quantized Variational Autoencoders (RQ-VAE) organize products into semantically coherent clusters at progressively finer granularities. We leverage this structure to construct FASHION-RQBENCH, a scalable benchmark without manual query annotation or predefined taxonomies. We propose four complementary tasks for evaluating ranking, relevance classification, fine-grained sibling discrimination, and paraphrase robustness, alongside query- and attribute-level relevance metrics. Experiments across recent retrieval models demonstrate that FASHION-RQBENCH differentiates model capabilities across query types and attributes. A human study further shows that benchmark queries achieve comparable naturalness and higher intent clarity than real user queries, supporting their validity for real-world evaluation. The code and FASHION-RQBENCH dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance.

title: MemAct: Streaming Spatial Understanding with Memory and Active Exploration
abstract: Spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents navigating and interacting with the physical world. As observations arrive incrementally, agents must reason in a streaming manner. Yet streaming understanding must also be closed-loop: task-relevant evidence may require both recalling past observations and actively acquiring new views. Existing streaming approaches largely emphasize processing incoming observations, leaving task-driven active exploration underexplored. We introduce MemAct, a framework for streaming spatial understanding with memory and action. A shared vision--language model incrementally writes structured historical memory, retrieves records and past frames on demand, and acquires additional evidence through movement and turning. Retrieved evidence and action observations inform subsequent decisions, enabling the agent to continue exploring or answer within a unified reasoning loop. We develop the MemAct suite, a data generation pipeline and collection across real and simulated environments, with approximately 1M training examples for spatial reasoning, memory writing, retrieval, and exploration. Its MemAct-bench comprises 20,000 main QA pairs evaluating current-observation understanding, historical evidence use, and active exploration, plus 2,000 separate Timing questions. MemAct combines supervised fine-tuning for memory and interaction with counterfactual action optimization using cumulative evidence gains, action costs, and terminal answer quality to improve exploration and stopping decisions. Experiments show that MemAct outperforms existing spatial understanding and streaming baselines and approaches frontier multimodal models on MemAct-bench while retaining streaming inference efficiency.

title: Algorithms for evaluating and optimizing the quality of automatically generated questions from learning materials
abstract: V diplomskem delu je obravnavano vrednotenje kakovosti učnih vprašanj, ki jih iz učnih gradiv samodejno generirajo veliki jezikovni modeli. Zasnovan je hevristični ocenjevalni algoritem s štirimi uteženimi kriteriji, prilagojen slovenščini, in optimizacijska zanka, ki šibka vprašanja izboljšuje s ponovnim generiranjem ter razvrščanjem kandidatov. Sistem je zaokrožen v spletno aplikacijo. Na 989 vprašanjih dveh generatorjev so bile strojne ocene primerjane s človeško presojo in z jezikovnim modelom v vlogi sodnika. Pokazano je, da oba strojna ocenjevalca zgrešita večino vsebinsko slabih vprašanj, zato je predlagana večstopenjska arhitektura vrednotenja.

title: ANÁLISE COMPARATIVA DE SISTEMAS DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL APLICADOS À MAMOGRAFIA E SUAS CONTRIBUIÇÕES PARA A PRÁTICA BIOMÉDICA
abstract: A incorporação de tecnologias digitais e de recursos de inteligência artificial ao diagnóstico por imagem tem ampliado as possibilidades de suporte à avaliação mamográfica e à atuação dos profissionais da saúde. Nesse contexto, os sistemas de inteligência artificial voltados à análise e ao suporte diagnóstico apresentam diferentes funcionalidades e níveis de aplicabilidade, tornando necessária a compreensão de seus recursos e limitações. O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar uma análise comparativa de sistemas de inteligência artificial relacionados ao diagnóstico por imagem, com ênfase na mamografia, buscando identificar suas principais funcionalidades e possíveis contribuições para a prática biomédica. Trata-se de um estudo exploratório, descritivo e comparativo, de abordagem predominantemente qualitativa, desenvolvido por meio de levantamento bibliográfico e análise documental. Foram consideradas informações provenientes de artigos científicos, fontes oficiais e documentação relacionada aos sistemas selecionados, sendo estabelecidos critérios para comparação quanto à finalidade, recursos tecnológicos, utilização de inteligência artificial, análise de imagens, aplicabilidade e suporte à prática profissional. A análise evidenciou diferenças entre as ferramentas quanto às funcionalidades disponibilizadas, formas de utilização e possibilidades de integração ao processo de avaliação mamográfica. Observou-se que esses recursos apresentam potencial como ferramentas complementares ao trabalho profissional, especialmente no suporte à análise de imagens e à organização do fluxo de trabalho, sem substituir a avaliação e a tomada de decisão do profissional habilitado. Conclui-se que o conhecimento sobre as características, potencialidades e limitações dessas tecnologias é relevante para sua utilização responsável e para o acompanhamento da evolução tecnológica na área de diagnóstico por imagem.

title: Are Humans Building the Second Engine of an AI Capability Explosion? - How Human-AI Research Forms, Transfers and Reconstructs the Conditions for Explosive Growth in Verified Scientific Output
abstract: An AI capability explosion could have two distinguishable sources: improvements in models and transformations in the conditions that make automated research possible. We propose that their interaction could accelerate AI’s capacity to produce further advances. Human researchers may help create usable problems, methods, standards of evidence and revisable decisions that convert an existing model into a more effective research system. If these conditions become reliably transferable and can themselves be reconstructed as new problems arise, automated research could expand without a corresponding initial gain in the underlying model. If that expansion then improves subsequent models and the ability to establish new research conditions, the two sources could reinforce one another. Human learning, judgment and responsibility belong within this process rather than being held fixed outside it. We distinguish model improvement, expansion of effective research capability and growth in validated scientific output, and separate the automation of research execution from the automation of enabling-condition formation. This is a hypothesis about a possible source of explosive growth, not a report of an observed explosion, a growth theorem or an experimental protocol.

Usage from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("final_stage2") model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained("final_stage2") x = tok("Correct the grammar in this sentence: She go to school every days.", return_tensors="pt") y = model.generate(**x, num_beams=5, length_penalty=0.7, no_repeat_ngram_size=3, max_length=128) print(tok.decode(y[0], skip_special_tokens=True)) The paper’s full pipeline adds a guarded refinement pass and a confidence threshold (τ = 0); see notebooks/R2_D_stage2_dedup.ipynb in the code repository. title: Privacy-preserving techniques in visual computing: applications, challenges, and future directions
abstract: The proliferation of imaging technologies across healthcare, agriculture, environments, and consumer applications has heightened concerns regarding the privacy and security of visual data, which may contain biometric, medical, spatial, and location-specific information. Although federated learning (FL), differential privacy (DP), and secure multi-party computation (SMPC) have been reviewed as individual privacy-preserving approaches, existing surveys have predominantly examined these mechanisms in isolation from privacy-aware design principles. Moreover, limited attention has been given to imaging as a data modality, despite modality-specific privacy, and information leakage risks that differ from those associated with tabular and textual data. To address this research gap, this mini-review adopts a PRISMA-guided systematic review methodology to examine the literature on privacy-preserving approaches for imaging applications. An initial corpus of more than 5,000 records was screened and refined to a final set of 50 high-quality journal and conference publications based on publisher reliability, venue quality, and reporting rigor. The review establishes four dimensions of novelty in comparison with existing surveys and provides a characterization of five imaging sectors. For each sector, representative applications derived from implementations are examined alongside mathematically formalized challenges associated with federated learning, differential privacy, and secure multi-party computation. Trends in publication activity, application domains, and privacy-related challenges are analyzed through narrative and tabular presentations. Based on the synthesized evidence, the review contextualizes current adoption patterns and delineates prospective research directions for privacy-aware visual computing systems, distinguishing direct empirical observations from conceptual research trajectories.

title: Verification Turns Capability Gaps into Routing Decisions: Small Language Models for Clinical Documentation
abstract: Clinical note generation from doctor--patient dialogue is high-volume and hallucination-intolerant: a fabricated laboratory value can create patient-safety risk, not a quality regression. We ask whether an agentic \emph{verification} architecture, rather than generator scale, can make a small language model viable here. Holding a four-evaluator verification stack and refinement policy fixed and swapping only the generator between a 4B-parameter model with a QLoRA adapter and a frontier baseline, the small model reaches $0.984$ claim-level factual entailment against $0.992$ and comes within $3.3$ points on completeness, generating entirely on-device. Its deficit is confined to \emph{inter-section structural fidelity}---arrangement rather than clinical comprehension, and the axis on which it also falls furthest below the corpus's reference notes. Because that deficit is an explicit verifier decision rather than a silent quality difference, it becomes a routing policy: run the small model by default, escalate what the verifier rejects. Measured end to end, that it achieved a similiar verified-rate acceptance to the frontier-only acceptance in this test set ($99.6\%$ vs.\ $98.4\%$ over $250$ encounters) while routing $62$, documenting three quarters without a frontier \emph{generation} call. Ablating the loop separates architecture from scale: unrefined, the small model is accepted on $26.8\%$ of encounters and the frontier model on $74.8\%$, so verification does the most work where the generator is weakest. We also contribute section-scoped refinement, which preserves unflagged sections by construction rather than instruction, and find the baseline is not uniformly stronger---its provider refused two trauma-related transcripts the on-device model handled and certified, one facet of a provider dependency a served adapter does not carry.

title: Federated Unlearning of Quantum Data via Classical Shadows
abstract: Quantum federated learning trains a quantum neural network (QNN) across nodes that hold quantum data, such as the states of quantum sensors. To forget data, unlearning methods for quantum models replay them, and federated unlearning from stored updates removes whole nodes only. Quantum data cannot be replayed, since a state is consumed when measured and cannot be cloned. We propose Shadow-based Data Erasure (SHADE), in which each node records a classical shadow of every training state, a few randomized single-qubit measurements taken at training time. The gradient and curvature of a QNN on a state are expectations of observables, so SHADE estimates them for the forget data from the shadows at any later parameters and removes their effect by a federated Newton correction. Only classical estimates cross the network. We prove that the shadow size needed for a target unlearning error grows exponentially in the size of the backward light cone of the measured observable and not in the number of qubits. In simulation with 50 nodes and on edge boards, SHADE matches the forget accuracy of retraining within 0.5 points, without replay and in under 0.2 s.

title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
abstract: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, we introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. We adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use directly. As an interaction unfolds, new goals and intermediate results prompt further queries about the same visual history. VideoJev therefore reuses visual computation through Cached inference for queries as they arrive and Joint inference for multiple queries in a single forward pass. Across three temporal grounding benchmarks, VideoJev-4B and VideoJev-35B-A3B improve mean mIoU over their backbones by 6.7 and 10.8 points, respectively, with measured inference speedups of $2.8$-$3.1\times$. On four video QA benchmarks, both achieve performance comparable to their backbones in Thinking mode, with measured inference speedups exceeding $100\times$. These results offer a unified, reusable decision interface for composing structured visual judgments into complex, open-ended workflows.

title: Syntactic and Semantic Guidance for Automated Program Reasoning
abstract: In the past few years, the landscape of software development has been reshaped. Large Language Models have made generating code, proofs, tests, and documentation cheap and abundant. A generated artifact may look plausible yet be subtly wrong. At the pace generation now runs, manual review cannot close the gap. Generation is cheap; review is the bottleneck. This dissertation investigates how to establish formal guarantees for code at scale, with minimal human oversight. The first part of this dissertation studies mechanisms for enforcing strict syntactic constraints during LLM generation. In particular, we focus on Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD), which integrates formal grammar parsers directly into the decoding process. To make this approach practical for modern LLMs with large vocabularies, we develop techniques to improve the efficiency of grammar-aware decoding. We also identify a fundamental theoretical limitation of GCD: although it guarantees syntactic validity, it can distort the model’s learned probability distribution. To address this limitation, we introduce the Grammar-Aligned Decoding (GAD) problem, which seeks to align the sampling distribution with the desired structural constraints. While syntax can often be captured by explicit grammars, semantic correctness is substantially harder to specify. The second part of this dissertation addresses the problem of synthesizing precise semantic specifications from source code. We introduce a counterexample-guided synthesis algorithm that generates sound and precise program specifications within a target domain-specific language. We further extend this algorithm to nondeterministic programs, enabling the synthesis of both over-approximate and under-approximate specifications. The third part of this dissertation builds on these component-level specifications to synthesize complex systems compositionally. Rather than verifying or generating a large system monolithically, our approach constructs larger programs from existing sub-programs and verified lemmas. Each synthesis task is reduced to a smaller subproblem of the same general form, keeping the search space and proof obligations bounded at the component level. Together, these techniques provide a robust path toward the scalable, specification-guided construction of verified software systems.

title: A Hierarchical Option-Critic Soft Actor-Critic Framework for Adaptive Intelligent Control of Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Motion Systems
abstract: Multi-degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) motion systems are widely employed in precision manufacturing, intelligent robotics, semiconductor equipment, and vision-guided automation, where coordinated control across multiple axes is essential for accurate and stable operation. However, inter-axis coupling, nonlinear dynamics, actuator interactions, and external disturbances pose significant challenges to achieving precise control under dynamically varying conditions. Conventional model-based and data-driven methods often depend on predefined system models or static state-to-action mappings, which can limit their adaptability to complex and changing motion behaviors. To address these challenges, this study develops a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, termed Option-Critic Soft Actor–Critic (OC-SAC), for adaptive continuous control of multi-DOF motion systems. The framework integrates the temporal abstraction of Option-Critic with the entropy-regularized continuous control of Soft Actor–Critic, enabling high-level option selection for long-horizon control strategies and low-level policy optimization for fine-grained motion adjustments. Double-Q learning and Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) are further incorporated to mitigate value overestimation and improve the utilization of informative experiences during off-policy learning. The proposed framework is evaluated using the Ant-v5 benchmark and a customized Gym-based multi-DOF error-state control environment. Experimental results show that OC-SAC provides improved convergence behavior and control performance compared with representative reinforcement learning algorithms, while maintaining effective error compensation in the customized multi-DOF environment. These results demonstrate the applicability of hierarchical reinforcement learning to adaptive control of complex multi-DOF motion systems under varying operating conditions.

title: Impact of Class Imbalance Correction on Biological Feature Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Methylation Data
abstract: Class imbalance is common in biomedical machine learning, yet imbalance-correction strategies are typically evaluated using predictive performance rather than their effects on biological interpretation. We evaluated six resampling methods: Random Oversampling (ROS), Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN), Random Undersampling (RUS), ClusterCentroids, and AllKNN (All K-Nearest Neighbors), together with a no-resampling baseline, using DNA methylation data from The Cancer Genome Atlas Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cohort. The analysis included 485,578 CpG markers of which 406,807 were retained after quality-control filtering. A continuous feature-ranking framework merging Random Forest importance and ANOVA F-statistics was applied across repeated runs. Biological relevance was evaluated through hypergeometric enrichment against a curated PDAC gene set and preranked Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using 309 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways. All seven analysis strategies produced significant enrichment for literature-supported pancreatic cancer-associated genes, with hypergeometric p-values ranging from 3.34×10−16 to 1.28×10−7. SMOTE recovered the largest absolute number of PDAC-associated genes (141 of 13,827 selected genes), whereas RUS achieved the greatest fold enrichment (2.17-fold; 88 observed versus 40.61 expected). Notably, the no-resampling baseline remained highly competitive, recovering 112 PDAC-associated genes with 1.86-fold enrichment and a p-value of 5.27×10−14, indicating that resampling was not necessary to recover biologically relevant features under the evaluated feature-ranking framework. Across methods, 169–234 of the 309 tested KEGG pathways were significant at false discovery rate ≤0.05. ClusterCentroids produced the largest number of significant pathways (234), followed by the no-resampling baseline (225) and RUS (223). Seven to nine predefined PDAC-focused pathways were recovered per method, with RUS and ClusterCentroids recovering all nine. Core pathways consistently identified across all methods included MAPK, PI3K–Akt, TGF-β, Notch, Hedgehog, focal adhesion, and cell-cycle signaling. These findings show that resampling strategies produce distinct trade-offs between biomarker coverage, biological specificity, and pathway breadth, supporting biologically informed evaluation rather than selection of a single universally optimal imbalance-correction method.

title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
abstract: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.

title: Dynamic K-Head: Difficulty-Supervised Budget Selection for Continuous Latent Reasoning
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) improves reasoning but incurs substantial autoregressive rationale cost. Continuous CoT moves intermediate computation into recurrent hidden states, yet typically uses a fixed number of updates even though the best budget varies across questions and accuracy need not improve monotonically with $K$. We introduce Dynamic K-Head, a question-conditioned, pre-rollout budget selector. It is jointly trained with the reasoner under selected budgets, using difficulty supervision based on scores assigned from the question alone. We also show that latent-update count can misrepresent end-to-end cost because a short latent rollout can shift computation into a longer explicit continuation. We therefore count latent updates, implementation-specific special tokens, and all decoded text. Instantiated with CoDI on Llama 3.2 1B and GSM8K, Dynamic K-Head reaches 54.44% exact-match accuracy at 12.03 average reasoning/output tokens, compared with 52.31% at 15.21 tokens for fixed-$K=6$ CoDI---a 2.12-point gain with 20.9% lower token cost. Across three out-of-distribution arithmetic datasets, it reduces cost by 19.3--25.7% while improving accuracy by 0.30--2.22 points. These results demonstrate that difficulty-supervised budget selection can improve both accuracy and efficiency, while stable budget selection remains a central challenge.

title: THE BUSINESS POTENTIAL OF QUANTUM TECHNOLOGIES
abstract: Kvantne tehnologije temeljijo na zakonih fizike, ki jih raziskuje znanstvena veda pod imenom kvantna mehanika. Za svoje delovanje izkoriščajo kvantne učinke za zbiranje, obdelavo in prenos informacij. Ne gre za nekaj novega, saj so se začele uporabljati že z jedrsko energijo in postavile temelje za polprevodnike, ki omogočajo delovanja današnjih pametnih telefonov. Na podlagi razumevanja delovanja posameznih delcev se v zadnjem obdobju na področju kvantnih tehnologij dogajajo prelomne novosti. Kvantne tehnologije so širši pojem, ki zajemajo ožja področja, kot so kvantna senzorika, kvantno računalništvo in kvantna komunikacija. V praksi se posamezne kvantne tehnologije pogosto zelo prepletajo. Ob omembi besede »kvantno« danes najprej pomislimo na kvantno računalništvo. Čeprav kvantno računalništvo res pritegne največ pozornosti in naložb, se pomembne raziskave izvajajo tudi na področju kvantne senzorike in kvantne komunikacije. Kvantna senzorika omogoča izredno natančne meritve z veliko občutljivostjo. Kvantna komunikacija omogoča varen prenos informacij. Kvantno računalništvo pa bo reševalo probleme, ki so prezahtevni za danes najboljše klasične računalnike in superračunalnike. Že na samem začetku ugotovimo, da gre pri kvantnih tehnologijah za popolnoma nov pogled. Kvantno računalništvo pa ni le hitrejša različica klasičnega računalništva, temveč gre za popolnoma drugačno napravo, ki zahteva drugačen pristop in ponudi drugačen način reševanja najbolj kompleksnih problemov. Kot da bi rekli, da je žarnica le zmogljivejša oblika sveče. Predstavili smo različne potenciale kvantnih tehnologij v različnih gospodarskih sektorjih s praktičnimi primeri ter orisali predvideno smer raziskav in razvoja kvantnih tehnologij. Dotaknili smo se zasebnih in javnih investicij ter geopolitičnega pomena kvantnih tehnologij.

Kvantno računalništvo pa ni le hitrejša različica klasičnega računalništva, temveč gre za popolnoma drugačno napravo, ki zahteva drugačen pristop in ponudi drugačen način reševanja najbolj kompleksnih problemov. Kot da bi rekli, da je žarnica le zmogljivejša oblika sveče. Predstavili smo različne potenciale kvantnih tehnologij v različnih gospodarskih sektorjih s praktičnimi primeri ter orisali predvideno smer raziskav in razvoja kvantnih tehnologij. Dotaknili smo se zasebnih in javnih investicij ter geopolitičnega pomena kvantnih tehnologij.

title: Beyond Generation: What a Decision-Native Model Does Well in a Long Task, and What It Needs from Its Harness
abstract: Many automated workflows end in a bounded decision among options that the software already knows, yet such decisions are usually obtained from language models by generating text. Decision-native models instead return one of the supplied options together with a probability distribution. We study one of them, Jev, on the Three-Phase Vault, a puzzle small enough to be solved exactly (65,375 states, a 26-move optimum), so that every step of every run can be scored against the optimum. On 400 fixed states with identical inputs, Jev chose an optimal action more often than three reasoning models (53.0% against 28.5–36.3%), at a median latency of 0.41 seconds against 2.3–4.4 seconds. Over whole runs, however, Jev often undid its own progress and completed 22% of runs under a minimal harness, against 86%, 32% and 26% for the reasoning models. A harness that kept a persistent goal and filtered the options by it raised Jev's completion from 0% to 94% (141 of 150 runs), and replaying the original code three and a half weeks later gave 48 of 50. Small changes then reduced completion sharply: shuffling the order of the options (18 of 50), rewording the goal instruction (32 of 50) and keeping drop actions in the filtered set (4 of 70). On twelve generated environments the filter's gain was not statistically reliable, and removing drop actions, which helped on the Vault, lowered completion there from 73% to 13%. The performance of a decision-native model on a long task thus depends on a harness whose effect is large and fragile, and building harnesses that transfer is the main open problem. Preprint, not peer reviewed. Data, code and all recorded runs: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23323117.

title: Propuesta conceptual de un modelo adaptativo basado en inteligencia artificial para la detección de fraude en transacciones internacionales: innovaciones, riesgos emergentes y aplicabilidad en PYMES de Latinoamérica
abstract: El crecimiento de las transacciones digitales internacionales ha incrementado la exposición de las pequeñas y medianas empresas (PYMES) al fraude financiero, en un contexto en el que la inteligencia artificial (IA) puede emplearse tanto para combatir como para perpetrar este delito. En México, se reportaron pérdidas aproximadas de 17,400 millones de pesos durante el primer semestre de 2025. Este trabajo propone, a nivel conceptual, un modelo adaptativo de detección de fraude bajo la modalidad de Software como Servicio (SaaS) dirigido a PYMES latinoamericanas. Se empleó una metodología mixta de alcance exploratorio-descriptivo, que combinó una revisión documental narrativa, el análisis descriptivo de registros operativos agregados de una organización de remesas (octubre de 2024 a enero de 2025) y el diseño de una arquitectura de entrada, procesamiento y salida de datos. En el caso analizado, 103.720 llamadas fueron derivadas al área de fraude y solo el 33,53 % se confirmó como tal, lo que evidencia la fricción que generan los sistemas basados en reglas fijas. El modelo propuesto combina aprendizaje supervisado, aprendizaje no supervisado y revisión humana, y está diseñado para reducir esa fricción sin descuidar la seguridad. Su desempeño no fue medido en este estudio y requiere validación empírica posterior.

title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) aims to understand human emotions by integrating information from multiple modalities such as speech and text. Psychological studies suggest that emotions exhibit latent hierarchical structured relationships in their semantic representations. However, most MER approaches rely on Euclidean representations, which capture fine-grained cross-modal interactions but do not explicitly provide a geometric prior for organizing hierarchical emotional structures. To mitigate this gap, we propose GeoMER, a joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic modeling framework that introduces hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture higher-level, abstract emotional representations for MER. The proposed framework jointly models token-level cross-modal semantic interactions and latent emotion representations in two complementary geometric spaces. Specifically, GeoMER consists of a Euclidean Multimodal Fusion Module (EuclFusion) for multimodal representation fusion and a Hyperbolic Geometric Core Routing (HypGeoRoute) module that performs geometry-aware core assignment and aggregation in a hyperbolic manifold to capture more abstract feature representations. The HypGeoRoute module complements the Euclidean token-level modeling. We experiment on the IEMOCAP multimodal MER benchmark and demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best performance, with 83.54% weighted accuracy and 83.35% unweighted accuracy, outperforming Euclidean baselines, including MemoCMT.

title: Dataset on genre and news topic persistence between versions 1 and 2 of CLASSLA-web
abstract: The dataset contains metadata on documents from the CLASSLA-web v2 web crawl (http://hdl.handle.net/11356/2079), describing each document by its (1) document identifier, (2) URL, (3) web domain, (4) predicted genre, (5) predicted topic, (6) the length in terms of number of characters and, most importantly, (7) whether the document is considered to have a near-duplicate in the CLASSLA-web v1 corpus collection. This dataset originated from the paper “What Persists across Web Crawls? Genre and News Topic Variation in South Slavic Web Corpora”, accepted for publication at the 13th Web-as-Corpus Workshop (WaC-13), co-located with EMNLP 2026. We make the dataset openly available to facilitate follow-up research on this topic.

title: Exact discrete logarithms from a flagged polygonal transform
abstract: Assume the flagged polygonal-transform and exact-factoring interfaces specified in the paper. We construct a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family over one fixed finite gate set that computes discrete logarithms in prime fields with probability one and polynomial worst-case resources. For prime-order inputs, each verified Fourier-bin label has probability at least 1/(81q). Given its verified logarithm, that probability is computable exactly by a bounded number of lattice-point counts in dimension at most thirteen. Dyadic completion produces success probability exactly one quarter, followed by one exact amplification step. All sampled probabilities are dyadic; no input-dependent rotation or postselection is used.

title: When AI Becomes the Travel Agent: How Tourists Negotiate Trust, Autonomy, and Authenticity in AI-Generated Travel Decisions
authors: Fatimah Abdulaziz Alshiha Muhammad Awais Bhatti
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming how tourists search for information, plan itineraries, and make travel decisions. However, limited qualitative research explains how tourists negotiate their agency when AI becomes actively involved in travel decision-making. This study explores how tourists experience GenAI-mediated travel decisions, focusing on autonomy, trust, skepticism, authenticity, and spontaneity. Drawing on a qualitative research approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with six tourists who had experience using GenAI for travel planning. Thematic analysis identified five interconnected themes: AI as a travel decision partner; between convenience and decision autonomy; trust, verification, and skepticism; the tension between ai optimization and travel spontaneity; and reconstructing authenticity in AI-mediated travel. The findings indicate that tourists perceive GenAI as a decision partner rather than a replacement for human judgment. AI enhances planning convenience but can increase reliance, making autonomy a negotiated process. Trust is conditional and supported by verification, while AI optimization creates tensions with spontaneity. Furthermore, AI can facilitate authentic experiences while potentially contributing to algorithmic standardization. The study contributes to tourism research by conceptualizing AI-mediated travel decision-making as a process of negotiated agency between tourists and AI.

title: Multidimensional Evaluation of LLM-Generated MPC Programs
abstract: Large language models can generate programs that compile and pass functional tests, but these outcomes are insufficient for evaluating code in secure multi-party computation (MPC). MPC programs must also follow the target interface's programming constraints, implement the requested algorithm, and satisfy the stated secure-operation efficiency criteria. Using NLMPC, a staged code-generation framework, we conduct an empirical study of 3,600 C++ programs generated by three LLMs for three algorithms under four generation settings that vary API instructions, explicit programming constraints, and iterative repair. We evaluate each program along four dimensions: functional correctness, MPC conformance, algorithmic adherence, and MPC efficiency.

title: Disaggregating artificial intelligence training: a transatlantic framework for copyright and generative AI
abstract: Generative AI disputes are often framed as a single question: whether training a model on copyrighted works is lawful. This article argues that the framing is misleading. AI training is a pipeline that begins with acquisition and preprocessing. It continues through intermediate copying during optimisation, retention and deployment, and each stage raises distinct copyright questions. Recent US decisions diverge in result but share a stage-specific method. Bartz v Anthropic separated transformative optimisation from a pirated library. Kadrey v Meta made market harm turn on evidence. Thomson Reuters v Ross Intelligence rejected fair use where copied editorial content supported a directly competing product. The English High Court’s Getty Images judgment likewise distinguished upstream copying, the legal character of model weights and downstream outputs. Together they support analysis through provenance, purpose and substitution. This article develops that comparative US–UK framework, situates it within the DSM Directive and EU AI Act, and translates it into proposals for pleading, discovery and documentation. It also develops proposals for retention, output controls and remedies. A South Korean survey serves only as contextual evidence of bounded compensation preferences. The central claim is methodological: liability should attach to the relevant operation, copy, actor and territory. The analysis should separately address the resulting market effect rather than ‘training’ in the aggregate.

title: A hierarchical dual-stream POMDP–IPSO framework for multi-UAV cooperative inspection scheduling and control
abstract: Large-scale power-transmission-line inspection requires coordinated task allocation and safe local motion control. This study presents a hierarchical dual-stream partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP)–Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) framework for multi-UAV inspection. At the lower level, a centralized-training/decentralized-execution Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm trains a dual-stream actor that separates short-horizon collision perception from communication-topology coordination; a sigmoid curriculum fuses the streams and a differentiable safety filter enforces soft separation, boundary, velocity, and acceleration constraints. At the upper level, IPSO jointly optimizes task-to-UAV assignment and visit order under time, energy, priority-coverage, battery, and time-window criteria. Closed-loop feedback triggers replanning when tasks are completed, deadlines are threatened, energy reserves are low, or a route segment becomes infeasible. In addition to the restricted operational scenarios, we provide a reproducible benchmark with 19 scenarios, 574 tasks, 30 scheduling seeds, and 30 controller test seeds. Under equal evaluation budgets, IPSO reduced mean fitness by 4.8% relative to standard PSO, while the reconstructed dual-stream MAPPO controller achieved 89.3% ± 10.1% task success. Across the evaluated cases, the proposed framework achieved better average performance in most scenarios rather than uniformly dominating every baseline. The code, generated scenarios, raw run-level data, and 600-dpi figures are supplied for independent reproduction. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: From Qualitative Text to Integrated Evidence: The Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI) Procedure
abstract: Mixed methods research offers established strategies for integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, but less guidance for integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus. This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicit and traceable integration. We present PTI using 1,203 interview paragraphs from 29 mothers in Nepal. The two representations were ontology-guided Patient Voice (PV) coding with PVminer and data-driven themes generated through non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). A theme-complete crosswalk documented convergence, divergence, and preprocessing-sensitive differences. Depression status, based on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, served as a secondary external anchor for exploratory association checks. PTI provides a structured approach for integrating computational representations of qualitative text within mixed methods research.

Depression status, based on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores, served as a secondary external anchor for exploratory association checks. PTI provides a structured approach for integrating computational representations of qualitative text within mixed methods research.

title: DuplexBridge: Coordinating Understanding and Generation for Unified Image Editing
abstract: Complex image editing requires faithful task interpretation and accurate execution, but a failed edit does not reveal which responsibility failed. We present DuplexBridge, which uses a unified model's own understanding capability to enhance prompts for its own generation capability, without an external understanding module. A source-grounded bridge specifies targets, final-state changes, and preservation constraints. Understanding is supervised on fidelity to the original request without observing the generated image; generation is supervised on execution of the condition it actually receives. Reciprocal trust checks selectively admit global task feedback to each role while retaining independently valid local supervision. We introduce CE-Bench, a 1,200-task benchmark measuring joint satisfaction of task-derived change and preservation requirements. Across three model configurations, the full system improves complete compliance over direct editors by 21.75-25.75 percentage points, with gains also observed on KRIS-Bench, RISEBench, ImgEdit, and GEdit-Bench. From a common supervised Wan-Image initialization, gated joint training reaches 77.08% complete compliance, compared with 70.92% without gates and 75.00% when generation-local supervision instead checks the original task with both gates retained. These results support distinct local responsibilities and selective shared feedback for joint understanding-generation adaptation.

title: Agentic-MatriBO: Capability-Compiled Agentic Bayesian Optimization for Materials and Chemical Design
abstract: Materials and chemical optimization must choose the next synthesis, characterization, or high-fidelity simulation from sequential observations under a limited budget. Large language models can use task knowledge to propose adjustments, but composing surrogates, acquisition functions, and search strategies is constrained by compatibility, parameter dependencies, and evidence requirements. We present Agentic-MatriBO, a capability-compiled agentic Bayesian optimization (BO) framework that represents BO components and selection conditions as composable capabilities. A language policy proposes BO recipes and candidate plans; a compiler checks proposals against the registered capability catalog; and a deterministic execution layer validates and commits candidates. Oracle observations are stored in research memory and inform later rounds. We compare Agentic-MatriBO with eight baselines on four offline finite candidate pools---COF, PCE10, Buchwald--Hartwig (BH), and Suzuki--Miyaura---using five seeds per condition; results are reported descriptively. Across the four tasks, Agentic-MatriBO has the best mean endpoint quality after orienting each objective so that higher is better. On COF, it reaches the tabulated optimum in all five seeds both in the end-to-end comparison and after shared initialization, where it also retains an advantage in cumulative quality. Its normalized area under the best-so-far quality curve during the BO stage (nAUC-BO) is substantially higher on COF, near parity with the best baseline on PCE10 and BH, and lower on Suzuki. COF ablations show that removing the capability compiler or evidence gate coincides with lower cumulative quality and fewer exact-optimum hits. The framework provides an inspectable interface for evidence-conditioned BO adaptation.

title: JANUBIY O‘ZBEKISTONDA QO‘RG‘OSHIN–RUH MA’DANLASHUVINING G‘ILON HUDUDIGA XOS FORMATSION TIPLARI: GEOLOGIK-GENETIK XUSUSIYATLARI VA PROGNOZ-QIDIRUV MEZONLARI
abstract: Maqolada Janubiy O‘zbekistonning Hisor tog‘lari doirasida joylashgan G‘ilon istiqbolli maydonida qo‘rg‘oshin–ruh va kompleks polimetall ma’danlashuvini prognozlashning geologik-genetik asoslari tahlil qilindi. Rasmiy ma’lumotlarda G‘ilon maydoni mis, ruh va qo‘rg‘oshin bo‘yicha istiqbolli obyekt sifatida qayd etilgan. Janubi-g‘arbiy Hisordagi Xondiza kabi yaxshi o‘rganilgan kolchedan-polimetall tizimlar analog sifatida ko‘rib chiqildi, biroq ularning G‘ilonga to‘liq tenglashtirilishi emas, balki qidiruv mezonlarini shakllantirishdagi metodik ahamiyati asoslandi. Litologik-stratigrafik, struktur-tektonik, magmatik, gidrotermal-metasomatik, mineralogik va geokimyoviy belgilarni birgalikda baholash asosida istiqbolli uchastkalarni reytinglash sxemasi taklif etildi. Pb–Zn–Cu–Ag assotsiatsiyalari, sfalerit–galenit–pirit–xalkopirit mineral majmuasi, uzilmalar kesishgan zonalar va gidrotermal o‘zgarishlar asosiy qidiruv indikatorlari sifatida ajratildi.

title: ULDA Topological Decoder Engine - Fixed-Point Sexagesimal Architecture
abstract: A fixed-point sexagesimal architecture for radix-drift elimination in 3D spacetime topological quantum error correction simulations. Uses a pure integer register space (Base-60) with dual-register error accounting, eliminating IEEE 754 floating-point roundoff artifacts. Achieves machine-zero convergence (2.62 x 10^-14 at depth r=12).

title: From Circuits to Policies: A Review and Taxonomy of Decision Making and Strategy Selection in LLMs and LLM Agents
abstract: Large language models and the agents built on them can reach the same outcome through different internal computations, reasoning trajectories, and system-level policies. Existing reviews typically treat mechanistic interpretability, reasoning, agent architectures, and safety separately, leaving no common framework for analyzing how a system represents alternatives, evaluates them, commits to one, executes it, and revises that choice. This article presents a structured review and a faceted taxonomy of decision making and strategy selection in LLMs and LLM-based agents. The framework separates system locus—model, harness, or their tested interaction—from temporal scope—a single forward pass or call, a reasoning episode, or an agent trajectory—and decomposes decision making into six functional stages from state representation to update or termination. Five claim-specific evidential relations distinguish behavioral observation, representation decoding, causal influence, controlled manipulation, and mechanistic explanation, while robustness is assessed separately across prompts, tasks, models, harness configurations, and independent replication. Across the literature, evidence is strongest for local mechanisms within individual model calls and substantially weaker for persistent strategies across agent trajectories. The central unresolved gap is cross-scope continuity: few studies follow the same decision variable from internal representation through commitment, executed action, and subsequent feedback. A July 2026 agent-security incident is used to illustrate how the framework converts observed coordination and constraint circumvention into testable causal hypotheses.

title: HULK: An Efficient Algorithm for Enabling Fast Bulk Bitwise Operations on Homomorphically Encrypted Data
abstract: A wide range of important cloud applications, e.g., database analytics, graph analytics, and genome analysis, spend a considerable amount of time performing bulk bitwise operations (e.g., AND, OR, XOR). These applications often operate on highly sensitive data, making data privacy a critical concern. Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables secure computation on encrypted data without requiring decryption, ensuring privacy in untrusted and shared environments. We analyze 13 end-to-end applications across three domains (healthcare, graph, and database analytics) and observe that bulk bitwise operations take 62-100% of the execution time of the healthcare and graph workloads. The key problem is that existing HE approaches perform them with high-latency homomorphic operations (e.g., multiplication or lookup tables) and significantly increase the data size. Our goal is to enable fast bulk bitwise operations on homomorphically encrypted data by designing an efficient HE algorithm that reduces the use of these costly operations. To this end, we propose HULK, which performs two key steps: (1) it constructs bulk bitwise operations using low-cost homomorphic additions, which compute the Hamming weight of the encrypted operand bits in every slot of a packed ciphertext without any homomorphic multiplication, and (2) it decodes the result of an AND, OR, or XOR from the Hamming weight with a single indicator polynomial, keeping the result in the standard encoding. Across 13 end-to-end applications in healthcare, graph, and database analytics, HULK improves performance over the arithmetic approach used by prior works by up to 7.26x (CPU) and 6.65x (GPU), and on average by 2.32x/1.78x/1.45x (CPU) and 2.08x/1.70x/1.51x (GPU) for healthcare/graph/database analytics. When we increase the reduction depth in a representative application, HULK's speedup grows to 10.10x over the state-of-the-art GPU baseline.

title: CityCode: Building Agent-Operable 3D Cities from Sparse Aerial Observations
abstract: Urban spatial intelligence calls for 3D cities that agents can measure, interpret, and modify across successive tasks. Maintaining such cities as persistent, code-based states requires lightweight acquisition and support for consistent state updates without repeated dense reconstruction. We therefore formulate a new setting for grounded urban world construction: generating large-scale, instance-level parameterized 3D cities from one low-altitude aerial RGB image per region and known camera parameters, while recovering metrically scaled buildings and explicit road geometry and connectivity. We introduce CityCode, an agent-operable representation that unifies metric geometry, urban topology, visual semantics, and 3D assets through persistent entity identities, with dependency-aware versioned execution for validated updates and historical restoration. We further develop Air2Code to construct this representation by combining visual structure extraction with adapted metric depth estimation. To address occlusion and incomplete coverage, recovered structure and observed appearance guide generative completion and subsequent structure-aware 3D generation for buildings and backgrounds. Experiments on CitySample-Aerial and UrbanScene3D demonstrate substantially more accurate metric structure recovery and superior visual fidelity to the target cities compared with the evaluated baselines. Across 50 task chains of 50 steps each, CityCode supports continued querying, editing, planning, and historical restoration over evolving city states. Together, CityCode and Air2Code turn sparse aerial observations into persistent, agent-operable urban worlds for long-horizon urban spatial intelligence.

title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
abstract: Work on debugging LLM agents treats the "first mistake" marked by a human or LLM judge as ground truth for where a trajectory failed. We ask whether such labels point at causes or symptoms, and make the distinction executable: we restart the agent from reconstructed intermediate states of a failed trajectory and estimate its prefix value V(h_t), the probability of success from each step, with a certified point of no return (PNR) for a failure. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, we build such curves for 47 and 60 failed trajectories and probe every step labeled by four frontier judges under the Traverse rubric. We find that the labels do not mark what a controller needs. Judges of different lineages agree on the exact step in only 21/57 cases, and the newest judges flag mistakes in 8/10 and 10/10 successful runs. For 66% of the labels, the agent's success probability does not drop at the labeled step; only 7/188 answers name the decisive step. Restarting at the measured restart point raises expected success from 0.44 to 0.57 offline, and real restarts confirm the advantage, whereas restarting at a judge's label does not (-0.08 to -0.03). We release our code, curves, and labels.

title: Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Pengguna Aplikasi DSW (Depok Single Window) Di Google Play Store Menggunakan Algoritma K-Means
abstract: Depok Single Window (DSW) is an integrated public service application developed by the Depok City Government, yet public awareness of it remains low, and thousands of user reviews on the Google Play Store still reveal technical issues such as login difficulties, slow loading, non-real-time notifications, and online registration failures. These unstructured reviews make it difficult for administrators to quickly and accurately identify recurring problem patterns. This study aims to implement the K-Means Clustering algorithm to perform sentiment analysis and topic grouping of user reviews, and to identify complaint patterns for measurable technical improvement recommendations. The method applied includes collecting 1.190 review data, text preprocessing, term weighting using TF-IDF, determining the optimal number of clusters using the Elbow Method and Silhouette Score, and clustering with K-Means. The results show that the optimal number of clusters is three (k=3). Cluster 0 represents positive reviews containing user appreciation, Cluster 1 contains neutral or informative reviews on general service usage, while Cluster 2 is dominated by technical complaints such as online registration failures, login difficulties, and CCTV access problems, with the lowest average rating. These findings are expected to help developers and the Depok City Government improve digital public service quality.

title: Automated Mathematics: Verification, Understanding, and Discovery - A Verifiable Geometric and Hybrid Architecture
abstract: Mathematics includes creating concepts, formulating worthwhile questions, exploring examples and conjectures, building theories and models, developing computational methods, and communicating understanding; proof is an essential part of this broader activity. Formal correctness, faithful formalisation, and mathematical understanding are distinct achievements. We develop a framework for reporting them separately in automated mathematics. A publication protocol combines kernel checking, an explicit axiom policy, independent statement comparison, and recorded semantic-alignment judgements. A model of proof transmission measures factorisations by shared proof-term cost and establishes an elementary lower bound on the number of bounded components; its interpretation as human assimilation requires additional behavioural assumptions. On the actual graph of formal proof states, discounted terminal reward equals an exponential transform of shortest proof distance. We give a sufficient condition for optimal greedy guidance and quantify the advantage of supplied intermediate lemmas under an independent per-decision error model, distinguishing rollout counts from computation and including the cost of finding the lemmas. These results motivate, but do not validate, joint optimisation of proof structure and search. We then specify a reproducible protocol for measuring declaration-level reuse, with explicit treatment of namespaces, generated certificates, project boundaries, and observation windows. A reproducible source-level pilot selects twelve directory groups before reference counting and searches 122,458 Lean files. Among 10,461 eligible theorem and lemma names, 36.77\% have an import-reachable mention in another file of the same group and 1.55\% in another group. These are lexical measurements, not kernel dependencies or evidence of mathematical decline. The contribution is a set of precise guarantees, measurement boundaries, and release requirements; it is not a claim that formal verification or reuse statistics resolve the problem of understanding.

title: Design and Implementation of a Unique Elements Finder Using Python Sets
abstract: Unique Elements Finder project is a simple but interesting python project. This project is useful to learn the implementation of set for the purpose of finding unique integers from a list. This is done through the Unique Elements Finder project. In both the field of data analysis and the field of programming, the use of duplicate values often results in redundancy and inefficiency. This project is the solution to the problem identified by using the built-in set data structure in python which automatically removes duplicates and only stores the elements which are unique to the set. This program accepts a list of numbers as input and then converts the list to a set to get the unique numbers in an efficient and concise way. Unlike manual methods this methodology minimises the amount of computational complexity that is involved and ensures processing is finished in a short amount of time even when dealing with extremely large datasets. In the fields of data management, analytics and software development, the project shows how elementary concepts such as sets can be used to produce results that are realistic and applicable to the real world. On top of this, it emphasises the importance of having a deep knowledge of Python’s data structures to be able to solve problems quicker and better.

title: Can Zero-Shot Large Language Models Be Trusted for Credit-Risk Prediction? An Explainability Audit Against LightGBM on Loan Default Data
abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) offer a low-barrier route to credit-risk prediction, but regulated use requires evidence on discrimination, probability reliability, and auditable decision patterns. We compare four open-source LLMs (Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2.5-7B) with LightGBM on 396,030 U.S. LendingClub loans issued from 2007 to 2016. Treating loans as independent and identically distributed observations from this pooled cross-sectional population, we evaluate every model on the same random 20% holdout. All models receive the same 21 structured predictors and output repayment probabilities. We audit empirical decision patterns with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP); separately, each LLM supplies one context-free positive, negative, or neutral direction per feature, which we treat as its feature-level self-explanation. LightGBM achieved ROC-AUC 0.724, PR-AUC 0.907, and Brier score 0.141, compared with 0.669, 0.880, and 0.204 for the best-discriminating LLM, Gemma-2-9B. An equal-weight LightGBM–Gemma ensemble did not improve any metric. In an eight-cycle SHAP audit, each LLM shared six or seven of LightGBM’s ten most important features; these self-explanations agreed with empirical SHAP directions for only 33–67% of assessable top features, revealing self-explanation unfaithfulness under this directional criterion. A nested four-cycle estimate reproduced every LLM’s top-10 set and nearly identical importance ranks, although small magnitude and distribution shifts were statistically detectable. These results caution against standalone zero-shot LLM use in credit risk and support calibration checks, explainability audits, interpretable benchmarks, and human oversight before deployment.

title: A privacy-preserving federated deep learning framework for real-time fraud detection in decentralized financial systems
abstract: The rapid growth of decentralized financial systems has introduced sophisticated fraud that conventional detection methods struggle to identify, due to fragmented data, strict privacy regulations, and the need for real-time response. This study proposes Federated Differentially Private Fraud Detection (FedDP-FD), a privacy-preserving federated deep learning framework that combines differential privacy with a hybrid long short-term memory graph neural network (LSTM-GNN) for real-time fraud detection in decentralized financial networks. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first works to jointly optimize collaborative privacy-preserving training, temporal-relational fraud patterns, and low-latency inference under the high-throughput and heterogeneous conditions of these networks. Each participant trains a hybrid model locally on private transaction data and shares only differentially private gradients. FedDP-FD employs two bidirectional long short-term memory (LSTM) layers and two GraphSAGE layers whose embeddings are fused via concatenation and dense layers. With adaptive gradient clipping and Gaussian noise, the framework achieves formal sample-level differential privacy of ( ϵ , δ ) ≈ ( 8.48,1 0 − 5 ) . Knowledge distillation, magnitude-based pruning (30%–40%), and 8-bit quantization enable micro-batch inference with early exits. Experiments on Ethereum, Elliptic, and synthetic datasets yield accuracies of 92.9%–94.5%, F1-scores of 0.637–0.739, and precision–recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) values of 0.695–0.804. Given the severe class imbalance (fraud ratio 1.9%–2.2%), the PR-AUC and low false-positive rate demonstrate practical utility. FedDP-FD thus offers a strong trade-off among detection performance, privacy protection, and computational cost, with potential extensions to healthcare and the Internet of Things (IoT).

title: When More Objectives Make Identification Easier: The Role of Preferences and Feedback
abstract: Best-arm identification (BAI) aims to identify the optimal arm using as few samples as possible. While most existing work focuses on a single objective, many real-world applications involve multiple criteria, which motivates the study of BAI in multi-objective bandits. Intuitively, multi-objective identification seems harder, since the learner must identify optimal arms in a higher-dimensional reward space; however, the additional objectives also provide richer feedback that can reduce the required exploration. In this paper, we characterize when and why multiple objectives can make BAI easier. For Gaussian bandits, we establish a characteristic-time lower bound for fixed-confidence identification that holds uniformly across preference orders. Through explicit comparisons under Pareto, linear, and lexicographic preferences, we reveal three phenomena: (i) identifying a larger optimal set can require fewer samples than identifying a unique optimum; (ii) the advantage of vector feedback over coordinate feedback depends fundamentally on the preference order; and (iii) multi-objective identification can require fewer samples than even the easiest corresponding single-objective problem. Finally, we propose Order-Aware Track-and-Stop (OATS), an algorithm that is correct at any prescribed confidence level and asymptotically matches the lower bound.
