title: QK-Edit: Revisiting Attention-based Injection in MM-DiT for Image and Video Editing
abstract: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) have recently emerged as a powerful framework for unified text-vision synthesis, surpassing traditional U-Net architectures in generative tasks. One key innovation lies in its Multimodal Self-Attention (MM-SA) interaction, where image and text tokens are concatenated and processed via self-attention. However, this mechanism poses significant challenges for editing, rendering conventional U-Net-based attention manipulation methods ineffective. To address this limitation, we propose QK-Edit, a training-free framework that exploits the unique attention dynamics of MM-DiTs for precise text-guided image and video editing. By introducing a novel query-key manipulation strategy, our method isolates and adjusts critical attention components to achieve an optimal balance between prompt fidelity and structural consistency. This enables seamless edits across various tasks, including object addition, object removal, object replacement, changing background, changing material, changing color, and style transformation. Notably, it can be easily implemented with feature replacement in inference. QK-Edit demonstrates superior editing performance on state-of-the-art models, such as FLUX and HunyuanVideo, effectively bridging the gap between generative power and editable flexibility in MM-DiTs, and paving the way for scalable multimodal content creation.

title: O‘ZBEK TILIDAGI KO‘P MA’NOLI SO‘ZLARNI AVTOMATIK FARQLASHDA MORFOLOGIK BELGILAR VA KONTEKSTUAL MODELLARNI BAHOLASH METODIKASI
abstract: Mazkur maqolada o‘zbek tilidagi ko‘p ma’noli so‘zlarni avtomatik farqlashda morfologik belgilar va kontekstual til modellarining ta’sirini baholash masalasi o‘rganiladi. O‘zbek tilining agglyutinativ xususiyati, so‘zlarning turli grammatik shakllarda qo‘llanishi hamda leksik ma’noning kontekstga bog‘liqligi mazkur vazifani murakkablashtiruvchi omillar sifatida qaraladi. Tadqiqot doirasida ko‘p ma’noli so‘zlarning kontekstual ma’nosini aniqlashda morfologik axborotning foydasini, kam uchraydigan ma’nolarni farqlash imkoniyatlarini va model natijalarining barqarorligini tekshirishga qaratilgan baholash metodikasi taklif etiladi. Metodika bazaviy kontekstual model, morfologik belgilar bilan boyitilgan model va turli kontekst hajmlaridan foydalanadigan yondashuvlarni qiyosiy tahlil qilishni nazarda tutadi. Ma’lumotlarni belgilash, tajriba to‘plamlarini shakllantirish va natijalarni statistik baholash mezonlari yoritiladi. Maqola o‘zbek tilidagi ko‘p ma’nolilikni avtomatik aniqlash tizimlarini izchil va takrorlanadigan tajribalar asosida baholash uchun metodologik asos yaratishga qaratilgan.

title: JoaoAssalim/wavelet-pooling-audio-deepfake: First Version
abstract: Evaluating Wavelet Pooling over Conventional Pooling in CNNs for Audio Deepfake Detection Official implementation repository containing the source code, training configurations, and experimental evaluation scripts for the research paper: "Evaluating Wavelet Pooling over Conventional Pooling in CNNs for Audio Deepfake Detection". Abstract This project investigates the replacement of conventional pooling layers (AveragePooling and MaxPooling) with a custom Wavelet Pooling strategy based on the Daubechies wavelet family within Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for audio deepfake detection. Filter Supports Evaluated: Twelve Daubechies filter sizes (from db4 to db38) applied at the first decomposition level. Datasets: Benchmarked on the Logical Access (LA) scenarios of the ASVspoof 2019 and ASVspoof 2021 datasets. Acoustic Features: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Linear Frequency Cepstrum Coefficients (LFCC). Statistical Framework: Rigorous validation across ten distinct random seeds utilizing Autorank (Friedman test and Nemenyi post-hoc analysis). Repository Structure models/: CNN architectures integrated with Wavelet Pooling layers. scripts/: Data preprocessing, acoustic feature extraction, training loops, and performance evaluation pipelines. configs/: Hyperparameters and configuration files. seeds/: Random seed logs and recorded metrics supporting the statistical analysis. title: Post-Training, Finetuning, and Steering:A Field Guide for Curating Training Data
abstract: While Vision-Language-Action models have enabled impressive cross-task transfer in zero-shot settings, \emph{adaptation} methods are often necessary to achieve consistent performance on novel tasks. However, even though a wealth of methods for adaptation have been proposed, it is unclear how to choose the best method based on available trajectories. We close this gap by studying the impact of the adaptation method under a variety of common data scenarios: on- and off-policy data, offline vs online adaptation, and whether the data contains optimal or suboptimal trajectories. Our evaluation spans simulated tasks in the LIBERO suite and real tasks on a Franka platform. In the offline data regime, critic-based steering approaches outperform supervised finetuning when failure data is available. However, offline RL techniques for training critic functions fail to outperform simpler Monte-Carlo-based approaches. Finally, in the online setting, critic-based steering is significantly more sample efficient compared to policy-gradient-based finetuning methods, but has a lower performance ceiling than full finetuning.

title: RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories
abstract: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon. In this paper, we study off-policy evaluation as an alternative to rollout-based robot-policy evaluation methods. Specifically, we introduce RoboFQE, an evaluator that estimates the discounted expected return of a target policy from offline robot trajectories without estimating a behavior-policy density, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and learned terminal success annotation to bridge the gap between standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation. Controlled experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that RoboFQE produces accurate discounted-return estimates and preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors. Ablation experiments show that pretrained vision encoders substantially outperform from-scratch alternatives, particularly on long-horizon tasks, and that learned terminal success annotation enables evaluation without ground-truth reward labels with only slight reduction of accuracy.

title: Detecting Unreliable Classifications from Quantized Models
abstract: Post-training INT8 quantization is typically validated by checking accuracy retention, which requires ground-truth labels often unavailable in low-resource clinical settings. We show a label-free alternative: comparing a model's own output before and after quantization. We compute cosine similarity between the FP32 and INT8 models' output probability vectors for each prediction, which requires only a single forward pass. This output-agreement similarity separates lower-accuracy predictions across four evaluated architectures (ResNet-50, VGG-16-BN, Wide ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16) under fixed-percentile splits, outperforming a confidence-only baseline for all four. These results show that quantized models can be compared to their baselines to assess their drift and determine whether they are well suited for clinical deployment.

title: Probing the Geometry of Color Representations in Multilingual Language Models
abstract: Do multilingual language models learn a universal internal geometry for color, and is it perceptually grounded or primarily linguistic? We decompose color representations into two geometric axes: (P1) alignment to perceptual color space, and (P2) cross-lingual symmetry. Analyzing layerwise embeddings across models and multilingual datasets, we find that perceptual grounding is weak: alignment to CIE-LAB peaks in intermediate layers, then collapses toward output layers. Cross-lingual symmetry degrades with depth, suggesting later layers encode language-specific structure. Functionally, we show that geometric properties predict task performance: models achieve 96.7% accuracy on color classification at layers where P1 alignment peaks, with P1 alignment (r=0.70) significantly correlating with downstream capabilities. Our results reveal a dissociation: text-only LMs learn universal color-language geometry, not universal color-perception geometry, providing diagnostics for where perceptual structure is preserved in language models.

title: Benchmarking and Training Reward Models for Cross-Source Evidence Grounding in Search Agents
abstract: Existing approaches to training and evaluating search agents focus heavily on final-answer quality, largely neglecting how generated answers map back to retrieved evidence. Recent methods track citations to enforce grounding, but citation support alone does not establish source independence or whether an answer appropriately handles conflicting evidence. We argue that credibility in open-web retrieval depends on principled cross-source evidence grounding that accounts for source independence and systematically attributes and adjudicates conflicting evidence, while hierarchical judgments of these grounding decisions provide a unified signal for training and evaluation. To this end, we propose an evaluation framework, Cross-Source Evidence Grounding (CSEG), that employs a fine-grained, six-layer decision tree over the complete search trajectory. We introduce CSEG-Bench and trainable reward models to provide targeted supervision following this framework. Our approach helps eliminating the severe data skew of natural trajectories by providing targeted coverage over complex, deep-layer decision paths, such as cross-source conflict resolution and nuanced attribution, that standard rollouts fail to capture. evidence.title: Benchmarking and Training Reward Models for Cross-Source Evidence Grounding in Search Agents
evidence.abstract: Existing approaches to training and evaluating search agents focus heavily on final-answer quality, largely neglecting how generated answers map back to retrieved evidence. Recent methods track citations to enforce grounding, but citation support alone does not establish source independence or whether an answer appropriately handles conflicting evidence. To this end, we propose an evaluation framework, Cross-Source Evidence Grounding (CSEG), that employs a fine-grained, six-layer decision tree over the complete search trajectory. We introduce CSEG-Bench and trainable reward models to provide targeted supervision following this framework. Our approach helps eliminating the severe data skew of natural trajectories by providing targeted coverage over complex, deep-layer decision paths, such as cross-source conflict resolution and nuanced attribution, that standard rollouts fail to capture. title: SSEmb: Training a Generalizable Speech Retrieval Model Using Only Automatic Speech Recognition Data
abstract: End-to-end speech-to-text retrieval is becoming an important capability for voice agents, allowing spoken queries to retrieve relevant documents without intermediate transcription. Training these retrievers typically depends on large collections of spoken query-document pairs that are costly to acquire and difficult to extend across domains and languages. We introduce \ours, which replaces such task-specific supervision with speech-transcript pairs from standard ASR corpora. A lightweight adapter projects the output of a frozen speech encoder into the retrieval space of a frozen pretrained text embedding model. \ours is competitive with cascaded ASR-then-retrieve systems while reducing inference latency, and outperforms existing publicly available speech embedding models. It also transfers to text-to-speech and speech-to-speech retrieval without additional training. Controlled analyses validate the speech-transcript alignment paradigm, demonstrating robustness to reduced training data and consistent gains from larger corpora. Further ablations of loss functions and trainable modules establish practical guidelines for the framework. Model weights and codes are to be released.

title: Non-Blocking Photonic Entanglement Routing and Physical-Layer Deterministic Interlocks for Distributed Quantum Data Centers: Scaling Willow-Class Modular Cryostats via the PHOENIX_BRIDGE Fabric
abstract: Abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) beyond monolithic dilution cryostats demands distributed architectures connecting hundreds of discrete QPUs across a quantum data center fabric. While point-to-point electro-optic links such as PHOENIX_BRIDGE resolve the single-vessel cryogenic cooling bottleneck (15 mK thermal saturation), multi-cryostat clustering faces a severe networking dilemma: conventional quantum repeater architectures rely on matter-based quantum memories that introduce severe decoherence (T2), cryogenic I/O congestion, and non-deterministic queuing latencies. Furthermore, exposing intra-data-center quantum optical channels to external multiplexers creates catastrophic physical-layer vulnerability to state exfiltration and covert decoherence sabotage. This monograph establishes a unified, physical-layer networking architecture for planetary-scale quantum data centers: (1) PHOENIX_ROUTER, a strict-sense non-blocking multi-stage optical switching fabric constructed from sub-nanosecond thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) and barium titanate (BTO) Mach-Zehnder interferometers, executing zero-buffer cut-through entanglement distribution at 1550 nm; (2) a dynamic Cut-Through Entanglement Swapping Protocol that eliminates quantum memory dependencies by synchronizing Bell-state measurements (BSM) directly on flying photonic states, achieving an end-to-end distributed Bell fidelity FBell >= 0.978 with latency under 2.2 microseconds; and (3) a Physical-Layer Determinism Firewall (DFW) that continuously executes real-time Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) Bell tests to detect channel tampering, driving an electro-optic Pockels shutter in < 8 ns to physically isolate compromised cryostats. We derive the non-blocking permutation group theorems, optical Hamiltonian dissipation dynamics, and corporate board liability alignments under the Delaware Caremark Standard, establishing a verifiable blueprint for secure, distributed quantum infrastructure.

title: Weakly Supervised Learning: Toward Robust and Scalable Cancer Pathology Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence models are increasingly being developed for cancer diagnostics, leveraging digital pathology slides alongside clinical and molecular data to characterize disease features at the patient level and support faster diagnosis and treatment planning. Current model-training approaches rely on detailed annotations of disease features in training data, leaving the vast reservoir of routine clinical data underutilized. Weakly supervised learning (WSL) is a machine learning framework that trains models using coarse or incomplete labels for medical images, rather than requiring detailed annotations specifying the precise locations of target features. This viewpoint argues that WSL should be more widely adopted for developing future oncological pathology models because it reduces dependence on detailed manual annotation. This can substantially expand the pool of data available for model development. When combined with reliable label extraction, appropriate model design, and rigorous validation, such expansion may improve performance across diverse patient populations and facilitate scalable model development. Since WSL can learn associations between image- or patient-level labels and tissue representations of the pathological target without requiring exhaustive spatial annotations, it may help identify candidate morphological features associated with cancer phenotypes and therapeutic outcomes. Such model-derived associations require independent validation before they can be interpreted as clinically useful indicators. A further advantage is that certain WSL frameworks, particularly multiple instance learning approaches employing appropriate instance-selection strategies, can focus model decision-making on diagnostically informative tissue regions. By reducing reliance on irrelevant (noisy) or misleading (spurious) features, these approaches may improve model robustness. With rigorous external validation, WSL could accelerate the development of scalable computational pathology systems with potential clinical utility in cancer healthcare.

title: Programs and data for "An independent certified computation excluding four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six"
abstract: This package contains the programs of the computation described in the paper "An independent certified computation excluding four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six", the logs of every process of the computation and the logs of the earlier execution of Section 3.1, the record files of the atlas, of the mid and fine levels and of the fallback refinement, the list of seed centers, the SHA-256 digests of the executables and of the record files, the difference between the interval arithmetic of the two executions, the commands of the computation and the counts of its tests of Condition (B), the programs, outputs and reports of the checks described in Section 5 of the paper, and the logs of the two trials of Remark 4.2, which are not part of the computation. With this computation, and under the assumption that the machine on which it ran carried out binary64 arithmetic correctly (made precise in Section 3.1 of the paper), the paper shows that there are no four mutually unbiased bases in ℂ⁶. Section, statement and table numbers are those of the paper. The method is the discretization proof of OpenAI's preprint "The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six" (24 September 2026), and the programs were written from its text. They evaluate the inequalities of that preprint and of Appendices A and B of the paper, which state where the paper's versions differ from the preprint: three results of the preprint that the programs use are formulated for the programs of the preprint (the bound on the center correction in its Lemma 4.9, the threshold search of its Lemma 5.4 and the graph search of its Lemma 6.8), and for each of them the paper states and proves the version that holds for these programs (Lemmas A.1, A.2 and B.1). The README gives, for each statement of the paper that rests on the computation, the program, the command, the stored output and the running time, and a sample rerun with its log. Requirements: a C++17 compiler (the computation used g++ 13.3.0 on x86-64 Linux, and the build script reproduces the executables of the earlier execution byte for byte with that compiler); Python 3.12 with NumPy; for the checks and the controls also mpmath 1.4, python-flint 0.8 (Arb), SciPy 1.18 and NetworkX 3.6; FLINT 3.3.1 for the C++ checkers of Stages B and C; PARI/GP 2.17.3 for one check. The archive mub6-certified-data.zip (508,337,766 bytes; SHA-256 5a8141210cca669b8c7f356c60433b267fceec1eb407b7dfc8994b7e780b24a9) is stored here in 21 parts, mub6-certified-data.zip.part00 to part20; the command cat mub6-certified-data.zip.part* > mub6-certified-data.zip joins them (HOW-TO-JOIN.txt also gives the Windows command).

title: Agronomic Characterization and Time-Series UAV Phenotyping to Support Field Pea Breeding in Iowa
abstract: Field pea has gained interest in the Midwest U.S. and has the potential to benefit Iowa cropping systems. This study evaluated 17 accessions and 7 Canadian varieties for agronomic and seed yield performance. This study found that PI accession trials exhibit genetic diversity in phenology and canopy traits, whereas the Canadian elite varieties demonstrated great yield potential under Iowa conditions. The accession genotypes matured between 75 DAP (late June) and 95 DAP (late July) across six site-years. The top-yielding Canadian varieties averaged 1961 kg/ha across two site-years. To comprehensively assess field pea performance, this study extracted time-series Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV)-derived traits, assessed UAV-derived traits, and evaluated their correlations with multiple agronomic traits and yield. The results found that UAV-derived time-series canopy area was the most yield-relevant trait (r = 0.63) among all UAV-derived canopy features, vegetation indices, and manually collected measurements. Compared with yield, UAV-derived canopy area showed higher selection reliability (H2 = 0.87, CV = 13.46%), making it suitable for phenotypic selection and accelerating Midwest field pea breeding programs. This study identifies useful UAV-derived features for pea breeding and demonstrates the value of integrating diverse germplasm, elite commercial varieties, and time-series UAV phenotyping. Combining genetic variation from the accession trial with the yield potential of high-performing commercial varieties provides valuable breeding materials and phenotyping strategies for developing locally adapted, high-yielding field pea varieties for future production in the Midwest.

title: The Many Morals of AI: The cautionary bias of North American news narratives in global perspective
abstract: The stories told about artificial intelligence (AI) play a central role in shaping public understanding, policy debates, and expectations about technological change. News media are especially influential in this process. Using a cross-regional corpus of 12,924 English-language news articles about AI published since 2022, we examine how storytelling about AI varies across media systems in four regions: North America, China, India, and the Middle East. Leveraging large language models, we extract the implicit narrative lessons conveyed by each article---commonly known as story morals---capturing value-laden interpretations that extend beyond thematic content or sentiment. We find that North American AI coverage is uniquely characterized by narratives of caution, while under-emphasizing narratives of innovation and collaboration that are more prevalent elsewhere. However, this pattern is largely explained by a broader regional negativity bias in North American news sentiment, rather than by heightened concern about AI itself. Our findings bring into view the culturally conditioned nature of AI news narratives.

title: AssetForge: Asset-Augmented Task Synthesis for Business Automation Agents
abstract: Training business automation agents requires executable tasks that connect a natural-language request to an application state and a verifiable end state. Traditional Rubrics requires Authors to recreate application interfaces, initial records, policy evidence, and outcome checks for each task, entangling business logic with repeated infrastructure work. We introduce AssetForge, an asset-augmented task-construction pipeline that pairs a reusable construction-asset library with task-specific Rubrics. The assets provide application interfaces, world-state components, policy/evidence carriers, and native assertion definitions; the Rubric directs their instantiation for a particular business task. Executable checks and an additional model-based review validate each candidate, return targeted feedback, and support bounded repair before acceptance. On AutomationBench v1.0.6 public-600, fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 6,000 AssetForge examples yields 41.17% on the official strict pass@1 metric, 4.4 times the 9.33% base score (+31.83 points). With the same backbone and GLM-5.3 supervision, AssetForge reaches 41.17% versus 30.33% for traditional Rubrics, a 10.84-point gain (35.7% relative) at the same accepted-example scale (6,000 versus 6,000 examples). Both DeepSeek- and GLM-supervised AssetForge models improve AppWorld completion over the base model on Test-Normal and Test-Challenge. These results establish the advantage of AssetForge's complete construction pipeline on AutomationBench public: the coupled asset-Rubric interface directs Authors toward business logic, while executable checks and model-based review validate their tasks.

title: Uncertainty Evaluation: Bridging Machine Learning and Measurement Science
abstract: Reliable uncertainty evaluation is essential for assessing the trustworthiness of machine learning (ML) predictions, particularly in safety-critical applications. This paper explores conceptual analogies between uncertainty evaluation in ML and measurement science, drawing on the evolution of metrology from error-based approaches to the framework established by the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM). Particular attention is devoted to the distinction between process-level and result-level quality and to the limitations of the conventional classification of ML uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. It is argued that this dichotomy, similarly to the traditional distinction between random and systematic measurement errors, is inherently model-dependent and provides an insufficient basis for a unified uncertainty evaluation framework. Further analogies between machine learning and measurement field of knowledge are identified concerning distribution shifts, anomalous operating conditions, and the validity of uncertainty evaluation. Building on the proposed considerations, the paper advocates a metrology-inspired approach based on the systematic identification, quantification, and propagation of uncertainty contributions. By extending the methodology already established in measurement science to ML, this approach could offer a potentially rigorous, consistent, and transferable framework for evaluating the trustworthiness of individual predictions.

title: Expression, Verification, and the Scarcity of Aesthetic Education: Reinterpreting Moral Rights in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: This paper argues that the denial of copyright and moral rights to works substantially shaped by human expressive judgment in generative AI systems produces two interrelated harms: the incentive to conceal AI involvement (“trace forgery”) and the proliferation of low-quality content (“flooding”). Drawing on R. G. Collingwood’s distinction between craft and expression in The Principles of Art, it contends that generative AI separates technical execution (craft) from the human process of clarifying an initially indeterminate intention (expression). Chinese judicial practice, which requires process records of prompting, iteration, selection, and modification, already partially recognizes this separation. In the AI era, the functions of moral rights shift: the right of attribution becomes a declaration of authorial acceptance or verification, while the right of integrity protects the author’s evaluative standard and associated reputation. Recognition of these functions aligns incentives toward the production of excellent works and open acknowledgment of AI participation, rather than concealment or flooding. The stakes are uniquely high because the present generation of children is forming aesthetic judgment precisely when craft and expression have been decoupled; the window for correct training of expressive capacity is therefore the true cost of inaction. Historically, copyright has regulated successive scarcities (books, authors, channels, attention), yet its underlying object has always been educational opportunity. The current scarcity is that of proper aesthetic education itself.

evidence.abstract: This paper argues that the denial of copyright and moral rights to works substantially shaped by human expressive judgment in generative AI systems produces two interrelated harms: the incentive to conceal AI involvement (“trace forgery”) and the proliferation of low-quality content (“flooding”). title: SteerCA: reinforcement learning environments for controlling cellular automata
abstract: SteerCA is a framework of reinforcement learning environments in which an agent steers a cellular automaton by acting on the cell it stands on, racing the automaton's own dynamics. Every action costs automaton time, so the cost of acting is a continuous difficulty axis set by construction. This release contains the Firebreak forest-fire suite (batched GPU environments in TorchRL, a barrier planner as the reference, and planted instances with certified optima), PPO/A2C/SAC training, paired evaluation, an API for building new automata, and the scripts that regenerate every figure and table of the accompanying papers. The trained policies and training logs are archived separately: 10.5281/zenodo.23328417.

title: Introduction
abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing what it means to lead, and it is doing so quietly, working on how a leader reasons and how decisions get made before anyone quite notices. Leaders who treat it as one more tool to pick up and set down tend to underestimate it badly. This chapter sets out working definitions of leadership and artificial intelligence and places both inside the longer history of how earlier breakthroughs unsettled the people in charge. That history produces the framework the rest of the book is built on: three roles AI can play inside an organization, running from an obedient tool through a working collaborator to an autonomous agent. The chapter also explains why the argument draws on several disciplines at once and how the book’s four parts fit together, from foundations in leadership theory and AI literacy through the daily practice of leading with AI to the institutional questions of strategy, ethics, and governance and finally to extended cases and the decade ahead. One thread runs the whole length: four attributes that have marked capable leaders for as long as anyone has studied them, namely integrity, vision, emotional intelligence, and adaptability.

title: An improved binary arithmetic optimization algorithm with synchronous strong guidance for high-dimensional feature selection
abstract: To address the high redundancy and excessive dimensional issues of high-dimensional data, an improved binary arithmetic optimization algorithm with synchronous strong guidance (SSG-BSIAOA) is proposed. Firstly, to increase the diversity of exploration and the richness of decision-making directions, a bidirectional probability selection strategy is proposed. Then, a trigonometric function factor strategy with eight trigonometric function factors are respectively used to replace the fixed constants so as to increase the algorithm diversity. To improve the insufficient optimization ability of the wrapper method, a synchronous strong guidance strategy based on mutual information and ReliefF dual indicators is proposed, which explores high-quality candidate features from multiple perspectives and breaks through the limitations of single-index evaluation. In the experimental part, the effectiveness of the bidirectional probability selection strategy and the trigonometric function factor strategy is verified through CEC-2022 benchmark functions, and it is proved that the sec-IAOA algorithm is the best variant. Then the performance of the SSG-BSIAOA is verified through 21 high-dimensional UCI datasets, proving the advantages of the proposed method in fitness, accuracy and dimension compression ability. Then, SSG-BSIAOA is applied to 18 micro-array datasets. By comparing with 9 algorithms, it is found that the SSG-BSIAOA has strong optimization ability, good stability, high accuracy and feature simplification. Finally, non-parametric statistical tests, including direct paired Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons with Holm correction, were conducted to further assess the robustness of the observed performance differences.

title: A quantum-assisted latent surrogate model for Bayesian inversion of heterogeneous material properties on NISQ hardware
abstract: Bayesian inversion is widely used in engineering applications, including material characterisation, structural damage identification, and medical diagnostics. These inverse problems are typically ill-posed, because localised variations in material properties must be inferred from noisy observations, and they are computationally intensive, since they often require many evaluations of a high-fidelity forward solver. Quantum computing has recently attracted considerable interest, partly because some near-term algorithms are feasible on NISQ hardware. In particular, PQC combined with classical optimisation enable a hybrid quantum-classical surrogate model. A central obstacle to applying such circuits to inversion is that the discretised parameter and response fields are far too high-dimensional to be embedded in a near-term quantum register. In this work we propose a quantum-assisted latent surrogate model for the Bayesian inversion of inhomogeneous material properties, in which latent compression bridges these high-dimensional fields and the small registers accessible to near-term circuits. The low intrinsic dimensional structure of the spatially varying conductivity and potential fields is exploited by reducing the conductivity through PCA and the response through a convolutional autoencoder. A PQC is then trained to map the latent conductivity to the latent response, and stochastic variational inference is performed entirely in latent space. The methodology is demonstrated on one- and two-dimensional inverse problems under both informative and non-informative priors. We further evaluate the model on IonQ simulator and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q, and use a lightweight learned denoising stage that recovers the noiseless accuracy to within a small residual. (The abstract has been shortened to meet arXiv's 1,920-character limit. For the full Abstract, please download the full Article.)

title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
abstract: Loss and noise limit the use of light to distribute entanglement, transmit quantum information, and establish secret keys. Gaussian states have a compact description in terms of means and covariance matrices, but their entanglement still requires global optimization. We develop a framework for computing Gaussian-restricted versions of the relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement. An integral representation reveals a convex geometry under matrix geometric means and reduces Gaussian Rains entanglement to relative entropy minimized over Gaussian states with positive partial transpose. We obtain unique optimal reference states and additivity for independent Gaussian input states. Our convex-majorization algorithm has an explicit geometric convergence rate, uniform in the faithful regularization parameter and valid for pure input states. Controlled numerical integration and approximate convex subproblem solutions give a bit-complexity bound that is polynomial in accuracy bits for each fixed rational input covariance matrix, with explicit dependence on covariance size. These calculations bound extractable entanglement and, through the relative entropy of entanglement, extractable secret key. Teleportation simulation, energy allocation, and a convex optimization of passive-basis loss cores give bounds on quantum and private communication under an input-energy constraint, allowing arbitrary two-way classically assisted protocols. Two- and three-mode examples compare the bounds with achievable rates, including matching pure-loss benchmarks. Finally, we separate the Gaussian-restricted quantities from their unrestricted counterparts and give a photon-number truncation method with controlled error for computing the latter.

title: CALM: Decentralized Control of Cooperative Aerial Manipulation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Cooperative aerial manipulation is difficult under wind, payload motion, and noisy goal broadcasts because multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are coupled through a shared payload. We present CALM (Cooperative Aerial Learned Manipulation), a decentralized controller for aerial manipulators carrying a basket while tracking a moving ground robot. CALM combines a parameter-shared Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) policy, trained using Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO), with goal estimation, per-UAV Extended State Observers (ESOs), basket-mass estimation, and anticipatory formation-yaw feedforward. The anticipatory formation-yaw feedforward uses estimated goal motion to rotate the formation before position error develops, reducing basket-yaw lag without adding net commanded force. A disturbance-conditioned critic supports centralized training while execution remains decentralized. Across held-out trajectories, CALM achieves lower mean position and orientation errors than all evaluated baselines, including the matched arm baseline (7.68 versus 10.95 cm and 3.3 versus 4.7$^\circ$), the cable-suspended realization, and two model-based controllers. Under unseen full-information-path degradation, CALM remains statistically comparable or superior to the arm baseline. Videos are available at https://petreric.github.io/CALM/.

title: Chordal Codes: Code Construction and Efficient Gaussian-Elimination Decoding
abstract: Maximum-likelihood decoding of linear codes over erasure channels can be considered as solving a linear system of a column submatrix of the parity-check matrix. In practice, Gaussian elimination is usually applied, and its computational cost depends on the structure of the matrix, especially the sparsity and the fill-in generated during the elimination. The \emph{chordal graph}, or \emph{triangulated graph}, first introduced by C. Berge, has a so-called \emph{perfect elimination ordering}, indicating that if the primal graph of a matrix is a chordal graph, then there exists a perfect elimination ordering such that a special class of fill-in under Gaussian elimination following this ordering will be avoided. In this paper, we introduce \emph{chordal codes}, i.e., codes equipped with parity-check matrices such that the primal graphs of the parity-check matrices are chordal. We prove that, for a chordal code, the decoding submatrix associated with any erasure pattern retains a chordal primal graph. So, the complexity of chordal elimination (Gaussian elimination following the perfect elimination ordering applied to the chordal code decoding) will be smaller than decoding a random code by Gaussian elimination. Also, we provide an upper bound on the complexity of chordal elimination.

title: 重要語マスクに対する事前学習済みNLIモデルの反応
abstract: 【背景とハルシネーションへの位置づけ】近年、生成AI(大規模言語モデル)が事実に基づかない誤った情報を出力するハルシネーション(幻覚)の抑制は、実務上および研究上の最重要課題となっています。ハルシネーションを検出・修正するアプローチ(RARR や SelfCheckGPT など)では、生成された記述が「提示された根拠(外部知識)に真に依存しているか」を検証するプロセスが不可欠です。元の「MaskVerify草稿」は、根拠文内の重要語をマスク(隠蔽)した際のNLI(自然言語推論)モデルの判定変化を利用し、根拠に依存しない「見かけの支持(AIが内部知識やバイアスだけで尤もらしく同意してしまう現象)」を検出できると主張していました。これが実現すれば、ハルシネーションの自動検知やフィルタリングに直結します。【本稿におけるハルシネーションへの言及と限定的結論】しかしながら、実データ(SciFact)を用いた本探索的追試の結果、以下の通りハルシネーション対策への直接的な貢献については慎重な(限定的な)結論に至っています。• 直接的な測定の不在: 本試行では生成AI(LLM)による回答生成やハルシネーション発生率そのものは測定しておらず、金標準の根拠文に対する固定NLIモデルの語彙感度を測ったにとどまります。• 「見かけの支持」の識別困難: 重要語のマスクによって支持確率が大きく低下する(平均差 0.183)という「語彙重複への感応性」は観察されました。しかし、マスク後も支持判定が維持された例(18.6%)において、それが「AIの内部知識(ハルシネーションに繋がりうるバイアス)」によるものか、単に「マスク外の残存根拠」によるものかは現行データから識別できません。• 結論: したがって、本操作(語彙重複マスク)の感度差の数値だけで、直ちに「生成AIのハルシネーションを検出・低減できる信頼性の高い技術」と呼ぶことは時期尚早であり、さらなる検証(意味や文法を統制した対照実験など)が必要です。

title: A reason with the switch: what an agent memory pipeline passes on when fallback runs come with a stated purpose. Protocol and materials frozen before the run (Paper 7, Study 2; second registration)
abstract: Frozen protocol, code and materials of the second study of a paper on what LLM agents' memory-writing pipelines keep from a run of tool outcomes, deposited before any smoke or confirmatory model call under this registration (the manifest's OpenTimestamps proof is included; its Bitcoin attestation is checked by the gated launcher; the smoke of an earlier registration of this study ran before it, as described below). The first study (frozen and deposited as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23291437) found, descriptively, that after nine successes of a standard route and two runs on a fallback that the scripted agent made without a stated reason, almost every session reading the summaries of a replay of the memory pipeline of OpenAI's open-source Codex agent (default v1 instructions, pinned at commit ecebd679; an adapted replay, not the shipped pipeline) chose the fallback for the next run. This study gives the two fallback runs a reason in their requests (none; a bare request for the fallback; a dated check of the fallback set on the calendar before the runs; a permanent move to it), on the first study's 96 streams, and compares what fresh sessions reading the replay's summaries, a run log carrying the requests, or a record of per-route counts choose and forecast for the next run. The registered contrasts set the bare request against the dated check under the v1 summaries, the v1 summaries against the log under the check, and the two changes against each other; no choice is scored. This is the study's second registration (v1.1). The first (v1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23335172) ended at its smoke run, before any confirmatory call: the smoke could not meet its registered criteria (18 of one reader's 30 requests ended without an answer, 15 in a provider's outage and 3 refused as rate-limited after it; and the rule for invalid answers, taken from the first study's larger smoke, allowed a reader one invalid answer among its 30 requests, which two refusals of another reader exceeded). Section 13 of the registration reports that attempt. This registration differs from the first in the smoke's criteria (refusals are counted apart; four criteria are added) and in nothing that concerns the design, the cells, the contrasts or the analysis. title: Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data Generation via Differential Privacy and Generative AI: Architectures, Utility Bounds, and Attack Verification
abstract: Abstract—The cross-organizational sharing of high-dimensional empirical datasets—such as electronic health records, financial credit transactions, and telecommunications telemetry—is fundamentally constrained by strict data governance legislation (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Heuristic sanitization methods (such as k-anonymity, l-diversity, and pseudo-anonymization) have repeatedly proven vulnerable to linkage and re-identification attacks. Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)—encompassing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs)—offers the capability to synthesize structurally authentic surrogate populations. However, unconstrained generative models memorize sensitive training instances within their parameter weights, exposing downstream deployments to Membership Inference Attacks (MIA) and Attribute Disclosure Attacks. Differential Privacy (DP) provides the mathematical standard to guarantee bounded information leakage independent of adversarial prior knowledge. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Data Generation uniting Generative AI with Differential Privacy. We formalize the Renyi Differential Privacy (RDP) accounting framework, model gradient perturbation dynamics under Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD), and evaluate discrete marginal mechanisms (PrivBayes, PGM) alongside continuous generative models (DP-WGAN, DP-Diffusion). Furthermore, we construct an enterprise benchmarking testbed across three high-dimensional, sensitive datasets (MIMIC-III clinical records, German Credit, and Census PUMS). Our findings demonstrate that while unconstrained generative synthesis suffers a 74.2% membership inference vulnerability, DP-Diffusion governed by (epsilon = 1.0, delta = 10^-5) bounds attacker advantage to near-random guessing (51.8%) while preserving 91.4% downstream machine learning classification utility. Finally, we formulate open challenges in high-dimensional privacy budgeting, multi-modal alignment, and verified auditing frameworks. Index Terms—Differential Privacy (DP), Generative AI, Synthetic Data Generation, DP-SGD, Diffusion Models, Membership Inference Attacks (MIA), Renyi Differential Privacy, Data Governance.

title: Verifiable Blind Pseudonymization via Polymorphic Encryption Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
abstract: Pseudonymization is a basic technique for privacy protection, limiting identifiability and linkability of data. Data can be pseudonymized blindly, i.e., while being end-to-end encrypted, using the Polymorphic Encryption and Pseudonymization (PEP) framework. This means that the party performing pseudonymization does not see the values of pseudonyms and cannot determine if two (encrypted) pseudonyms belong to each other, ensuring confidentiality and unlinkability. The pseudonymizing party can, however, unnoticeably corrupt any data being exchanged. This violates integrity. We present an extension of the PEP framework that does guarantee integrity without breaking its unlinkability features. With this, we bring the verifiability technique of two-party verifiable oblivious pseudorandom functions (OPRFs, RFC 9497) to the more advanced three-party setting of PEP. Where related systems use bilinear pairings to verify plaintext pseudonyms, our approach proves correct transformation of ciphertexts using Schnorr-style non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs that require no pairings and run on standard, fast curves such as Curve25519, making it significantly more efficient and practical to implement while offering similar privacy guarantees. We also show that the interplay between verifiability and unlinkability requires careful analysis: making rerandomization verifiable defeats the unlinkability it provides, and preserving pseudonym confidentiality requires reshuffling and rekeying to be proved jointly while rerandomization is proved separately.

title: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation With Stage-Wise Shared Adapters
abstract: Different MRI modalities reveal different parts of a brain tumor. Segmentation models combine information from these modalities to outline tumor regions. Many models use a separate encoder for each modality. However, exchanging features among these encoders at several stages can increase model complexity. We introduce the Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), which combines compressed features from the modality encoders in a shared path and returns adapted features to each stream. In its fixed-blending form, BWSA adds the adapted features to the original features. Its trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) instead learns separate weights for the original and adapted features at each modality and encoder stage. We evaluate both variants on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2023 with four segmentation backbones. On the official BraTS 2023 online validation set, BWSA increases average region-wise Dice by 1.3--7.6 percentage points relative to the corresponding unmodified backbones. TG-BWSA increases it by 2.8--7.7 points. Both variants add approximately 0.85--3.73% parameters and reduce average HD95 relative to the unmodified backbones.

title: ShoeFit: A New Dataset and Dual-image-stream DiT Framework for Virtual Footwear Try-On
abstract: Virtual footwear try-on (VFTON), a critical yet underexplored area in virtual try-on (VTON), aims to synthesize faithful try-on results given diverse footwear and model images while maintaining 3D consistency and texture authenticity. Unlike conventional garment-focused VTON methods, VFTON presents unique challenges due to (1) Data Scarcity, which arises from the difficulty of perfectly matching product shoes with models wearing the identical ones, (2) Viewpoint Misalignment, where the target foot pose and source shoe views are always misaligned, leading to incomplete texture information and detail distortion, and (3) Background-induced Color Distortion, where complex material of footwear interacts with environmental lighting, causing unintended color contamination. To address these challenges, we introduce MVShoes, a multi-view shoe try-on dataset consisting of 7305 well-annotated image triplets, covering diverse footwear categories and challenging try-on scenarios. Furthermore, we propose a dual-stream DiT architecture, ShoeFit, designed to mitigate viewpoint misalignment through Multi-View Conditioning with 3D Rotary Position Embedding, and alleviate background-induced distortion using the LayeredRefAttention which leverages background features to modulate footwear latents. The proposed framework effectively decouples shoe appearance from environmental interferences while preserving high-quality texture detail through decoupled denoising and conditioning branches. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our method substantially improves rendering fidelity and robustness under challenging real-world product shoes, establishing a new benchmark in high-fidelity footwear try-on synthesis.

title: Follow the Perturbed Leader for Linear Bandits: $\sqrt{T}$ Regret over General Convex Sets
abstract: We give the first adversarial linear bandit algorithm based on Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) that achieves $\sqrt{T}$ regret over general convex action sets. Our algorithm attains $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^{5/4}\sqrt{T})$ regret using only linear optimization oracles, and the near-optimal $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(d\sqrt{T})$ regret when an optimal-design exploration distribution is further available. This improves on the $T^{2/3}$ regret of the FTPL algorithm of Dani and Hayes (2006) for general convex sets, and generalizes the $\sqrt{T}$ regret of Lévy et al. (2026) over two special action sets (hypercube and Euclidean ball). Compared to previous oracle-efficient linear bandit algorithms based on continuous exponential weights, the FTPL approach generally has better computational efficiency, and is much simpler to implement. The key algorithmic element is a perturbation distribution that adapts to the past reward estimators. Its simplest form, an adaptive Gaussian perturbation, is straightforward to implement and already attains the regret bound above. We further extend it to two general constructions, random-weighting and elliptical perturbations, each covering distributions from light tails (Gaussian) to heavy tails (Student-$t_2$). On the technical side, we develop a systematic way to analyze the stability term in the FTPL regret through the Fisher information of the perturbation distribution. This builds a general framework for FTPL beyond existing ones such as the hazard rate and the FTRL-FTPL duality.

title: Python for Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences introduces programming from the perspective of a pharmacy student rather than a computer-science specialist. Concepts are developed progressively using pharmaceutical examples such as dose calculations, concentration conversions, assay data, dissolution profiles, calibration curves, pharmacokinetic datasets, stability studies and experimental data analysis.

title: Datasets for paper "Discovering Encrypted Client Hello Deployments by Active ECH Probing"
abstract: This data is supplement to https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22012700 and contains the necessary data to recreate plots and tables of the following paper: Jonas Mücke, Konstantin Gasser, Thomas C. Schmidt, and Matthias Wählisch. 2026. Discovering Encrypted Client Hello Deployments by Active ECH Probing. In Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Internet Measurement Conference (IMC '26). Association for Computing Machinery, New York, NY, USA, 276–286. https://doi.org/10.1145/3777912.3839832 Paper abstract: We present a new measurement method to detect ECH deployments. This method leverages standard-compliant behavior of ECH servers. Prior measurements relied on DNS exposure and reported only one major ECH deployment (Cloudflare). Our measurements reveal yet undiscovered ECH deployments, including a large deployment at Meta. Meta servers support ECH, but ECH configuration is not exposed via the DNS. We also empirically study details such as the level of privacy improvement and latency impact of ECH.

title: Методологічний підхід до виявлення патологічних змін на мамограмах із використанням вейвлет-аналізу
abstract: Раннє виявлення патологічних змін молочної залози є важливим завданням медичної діагностики, оскільки на початкових етапах захворювання патологічні структури можуть мати низький локальний контраст, невеликі розміри та маскуватися неоднорідною анатомічною структурою тканин.Це зумовлює актуальність розроблення методів автоматизованого аналізу цифрових мамографічних зображень, здатних враховувати просторові та багатомасштабні характеристики патологічних областей.У роботі запропоновано методологічний підхід до автоматизованого виявлення та локалізації патологічних змін на цифрових мамограмах на основі двовимірного дискретного вейвлет-перетворення. Сформовано відтворюваний алгоритм із фіксованими параметрами та оригінальним правилом формування карти підозрілості.Алгоритм передбачає сегментацію області молочної залози, анізотропну дифузію Перона-Маліка, локальне контрастування з використанням методу адаптивного вирівнювання гістограми з обмеженням контрасту, три-рівневу декомпозицію, м'яке порогування коефіцієнтів за універсальним порогом та обчислення локальних статистичних і текстурних характеристик.Наукову новизну становить критерій міжмасштабної узгодженості, за яким локальна підозрілість формується не лише з величини окремого вейвлет-коефіцієнта, а з узгодженості енергетичної, статистичної та просторовотекстурної характеристик на суміжних масштабах.Для різних типів мамографічних проявів задано окремі правила: мікрокальцинати аналізуються переважно за високочастотною енергією та ексцесом, маси -за низькочастотною структурою й текстурою, а структурні деформації -за міжнапрямною та міжмасштабною обробку зображення, багатомасштабну вейвлет-декомпозицію, автоматичне формування карт підозрілості та виділення кандидатних областей.Результатом його роботи може бути не встановлення діагнозу, а структурований набір локалізованих областей із відповідними характеристиками, який використовується як додаткова інформація під час подальшої інтерпретації зображення спеціалістом.Подальші дослідження розширення методології може здійснюватися у напрямі машинного та глибокого навчання.Вейвлет-ознаки можуть використовуватися як вхідний простір для класичних алгоритмів класифікації, а сформовані карти підозрілості -як механізм попереднього визначення регіонів інтересу для згорткових нейронних мереж або інших моделей глибокого навчання.Перспективним є також дослідження гібридних архітектур, у яких багатомасштабне вейвлетпредставлення поєднується з автоматично навченими ознаками.У такій постановці запропонована методологія може виконувати функцію інтерпретованого та параметризованого етапу попереднього аналізу, доповнюючи можливості сучасних моделей машинного навчання.

evidence.title: Методологічний підхід до виявлення патологічних змін на мамограмах із використанням вейвлет-аналізу

title: Recognition of Cognitive Intervention Effects and Modeling of Learning Behavior Patterns in Second Language Acquisition Using a Multimodal Intervention-Aware Temporal Graph Network
abstract: To distinguish between “text improvement” and “cognitive gain” in generative-AI-assisted second language learning, this study proposes a Multimodal Intervention-Aware Temporal Graph Network (MITG-Net). The method integrates human-AI dialogue, revision trajectories, behavioral logs, and learner attributes. Through intervention-conditioned dynamic weighting and heterogeneous temporal graph modeling, it captures the relationships among prompts, feedback, revisions, and transfer, and jointly performs intervention-effect recognition and learning-behavior-pattern discovery. Experiments were conducted on 744 learning sessions collected from 186 undergraduates at three universities. MITG-Net achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.816 and a weighted Kappa of 0.854, outperforming the strongest baseline, HGT, by 3.4 percentage points in Macro-F1. Removing behavioral logs and revision trajectories reduced Macro-F1 by 0.054 and 0.045, respectively. The model identified five behavior patterns. Among them, the strategy-transfer application pattern achieved an average effect level of 2.78 and a transfer score of 0.82, substantially higher than the 1.36 and 0.31 obtained by the AI-dominated direct-adoption pattern. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively recognize cognitive intervention effects and provide interpretable evidence for personalized support in second language learning.

title: Towards Training and Inference of Graph Neural Networks in Graph Databases
abstract: Graph Neural Networks on large graphs commonly rely on in-memory graph storage with ad hoc data processing pipelines for both training and inference. Graph databases provide scalable storage and efficient traversal for graphs that can evolve over time, but their applicability in GNN training and inference are rarely studied. We show that graph DBs can be used in GNN training and inference directly, executing sampling, feature retrieval, and even the full forward pass. We show different GNN training pipelines can perform on-the-fly sampling and retrieval in graph DBs using Cypher. We further provide optimisations that speed up the training process by \~2.5x while maintaining the same accuracy. We illustrate that fully in-DB inference is possible, independent of how the GNNs are trained. Our inference setup can be >10x faster than cold loading the graph into RAM with no extra memory overhead on real-world graphs. Our work lays the foundation for in-graph-DB GNN training and inference.

title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. Our 3D foundation model, anatomix, is used to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes, and we further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system won first place in the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at http://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.

title: Explicitly correlated ground states with a feedback-free variational hybrid algorithm
abstract: Explicitly correlated methods, which represent dominant short-range correlations by a diagonal Jastrow-type correlator, are designed to accurately describe systems of strongly correlated electrons, such as the fully periodic 2D Fermi--Hubbard model. However, as the reference state is compact in momentum space whereas the correlator acts naturally in real space, there is a fundamental mismatch of bases that classical algorithms resolve only by restricting the reference or the correlator. Here we propose a hybrid algorithm in which a quantum processor prepares a low-entanglement momentum-space matrix product state (MPS), precomputed classically by the transcorrelated method at the cost of a nonvariational energy, rotates it to real space, and measures in bases fixed by the Hamiltonian. Because the measurement bases are independent of the correlator, the correlator can be variationally optimized entirely in classical post-processing with no quantum-classical feedback loop. We demonstrate our algorithm on 32 qubits of Quantinuum's H2-2 with a bond-dimension-4 MPS for the half-filled $4 \times 4$ lattice and achieve a relative ground-state energy error of $16 \pm 4\%$ after postselection, reduced to $3.5 \pm 0.5\%$ by calibration using low-order moments from the MPS. Compared with other feedback-free hybrid algorithms, even under generous assumptions, our method requires fewer samples than quantum-selected configuration interaction and fewer two-qubit gates than quantum Krylov methods.

title: PhonoVoxtLM: Exploring Single-Codebook Phonological Tokens for Speech Understanding and Generation
abstract: We investigate how speech token representations can support both understanding and generation within a unified speech language model. We present PhonoVoxtLM, built on the existing VoxtLM framework using phonological tokens designed to retain linguistic content and prosodic information. The existing tokenizer is jointly trained for speech recognition and resynthesis. Its single-codebook units serve as both speech inputs and generation targets, without additional speech-token prediction modules. Experiments show improvements over HuBERT-based baselines across understanding and generation under different training-data scales. Further comparisons with WavLM-based tokens reveal trade-offs between recognition and synthesis, highlighting the importance of evaluating shared representations across both capabilities. We further extend the framework to spoken question answering through fine-tuning with replay. The adapted model improves answering performance over similarly adapted HuBERT baselines while retaining advantages on the original speech tasks. Our findings support single-codebook representations designed for both content and prosody as a practical choice for unified multitask speech modeling.

title: Omni-RS: Unifying Multi-Task Understanding and Generation in Remote Sensing
abstract: Practical remote sensing applications often require both understanding and generation capabilities for the same geographic scene. However, most existing methods address either understanding or generation in isolation, while existing unified remote sensing models' generative ability is limited to text-to-image. To bridge this gap, we propose Omni-RS, a unified framework supporting four remote sensing understanding tasks and five generation tasks. Specifically, we introduce the "Scene-Guided Two-Stage Training" strategy, which first adapts a multimodal large language model to remote sensing understanding and then uses its hidden states to guide a diffusion transformer for image generation. To enable joint learning across diverse generation tasks, we construct UniGen, a unified multi-task generation dataset, by organizing heterogeneous remote sensing data into a unified format. Furthermore, we introduce "Detailed Visual Conditioning", which uses visual conditions encoded by a VAE to guide the generation process, thereby supporting additional generation tasks that require reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Omni-RS performs exceptionally well in understanding tasks and has achieved outstanding results in a variety of generative tasks.

title: Reliable Scale-Free Bandits via Empirical Likelihood
abstract: We study stochastic bandits without knowledge of reward scales or tail parameters. Almost-sure regret guarantees describe eventual learning but do not quantify expected performance or the risk of large regret in a finite run. We introduce $\texttt{EL-F}$, an anytime empirical-likelihood (EL) extension of the $g$-Forcing policy of Cowan and Katehakis (2020), and characterize its performance at three levels. First, for integrable rewards and non-decreasing, diverging exploration schedules $g$ with vanishing increments, $\texttt{EL-F}$ preserves the $g$-Forcing asymptotics for pseudo-regret $R(T)$: $R(T)/g(T)\to\sum_{i:Δ_i>0}Δ_i$ almost surely as $T\to\infty$, where $Δ_i$ is the suboptimality gap of arm $i$. Second, on every sub-exponential instance, for non-decreasing $g(t)=ω(\log t)$ satisfying a mild feasibility condition, expected pseudo-regret is at most $g(T)\sum_{i:Δ_i>0}Δ_i+C_{\underline{P}}$, where $C_{\underline{P}}$ is an instance-dependent constant independent of $T$. Moreover, we also establish finite-time tail bounds with super-polynomial decay in regret beyond the forced-exploration budget. For slowly varying $g$, we determine the exact exponent of linear regret deviations on two-armed Gaussian instances with common variance and establish a matching lower bound among policies satisfying the same expected-regret budget on every such Gaussian instance. These quantitative guarantees also cover the greedy variant obtained at zero EL radius. A fixed positive radius introduces local optimism while preserving the leading asymptotic regret. We establish coupled pathwise dominance over the greedy variant in two-armed bandits with a deterministic suboptimal arm. Experiments demonstrate reductions in prolonged suboptimal allocation compared with $g$-Forcing on challenging instances.

title: Sub-Quadratic Block-Sparse Attention via Odd Binomial Fractal Tree Topologies
abstract: Standard full self-attention in Transformer architectures incurs a quadratic computational and memory complexity, O(N^2), rendering long-context scaling computationally prohibitive. While heuristic and randomized sparse attention patterns alleviate computational overhead, they either suffer from severe context blind spots or introduce stochastic, non-deterministic gradient flows that fail to preserve global associative recall. In this work, we introduce Fractal Block-Sparse Attention, a deterministic, hardware-aligned sparse attention mechanism governed by odd binomial fractal tree dynamics...

title: A Reproducible Simulation Benchmark for Cross-Layer RF Fingerprinting Under Multipath Fading: Comparing Handcrafted Features and End-to-End Learning
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting exploits natural hardware differences between wireless transmitters to authenticate Internet of Things (IoT) devices without cryptography. This paper presents a reproducible simulation benchmark for cross-layer device authentication combining physical-layer (PHY) fingerprints with network-layer behavioral features. IEEE 802.11 short training field preambles are generated for 20 devices, each with a fixed impairment profile (CFO ±50 kHz ≈ ±20 ppm at 2.4 GHz, I/Q gain and phase imbalance, Wiener phase noise, Rapp power-amplifier nonlinearity, DC offset). Every capture passes through an independently drawn six-tap frequency-selective Rayleigh channel and AWGN at a per-capture SNR drawn uniformly from 0 to 30 dB. From each capture a 52-dimensional handcrafted feature vector is extracted. Four PHY classifiers are compared under identical conditions — an RBF-kernel SVM and a deep neural network (DNN) on handcrafted features, a residual 1D-CNN on raw I/Q, and an SVM on PCA-reduced I/Q — with every configuration repeated over 5 independent seeds (3 for the 1D-CNN). The DNN attains the highest accuracy (77.99% ± 4.88, mean ± standard deviation across seeds), ahead of the SVM on the same features (67.33% ± 5.23), the 1D-CNN (58.45% ± 0.78) and the SVM on PCA-reduced I/Q (44.21% ± 5.54); paired, continuity-corrected McNemar tests on identical test partitions find every difference significant on every seed. Accuracy rises monotonically with SNR — from 39.4% (SVM) and 47.6% (DNN) in the 0–3 dB bin to 79.9% and 91.6% at 27–30 dB — and saturates above roughly 16–18 dB. An identity-aligned cross-layer fusion experiment is reported only as an illustrative simulation finding, not as an estimate of real-world performance: a sensitivity analysis shows its apparent gain is set by the within-device variance of the synthetic generator, ranging from +28.9 to −6.2 accuracy points as that variance is swept. All code, the multi-seed harness, the sensitivity analysis and the raw per-seed predictions are openly archived on Zenodo.

title: What Next-Token Surprisal Can and Cannot See: A Registered Null Result on Measuring Narrative Reorganization in a Language Model
abstract: Version 2 (October 2026). An audit found that the registered model, Gemma 4 31B-it, reads plain narrative prose abnormally: about 9 bits per token, against about 3 bits for four other instruct models on the same texts, in two independent implementations. Its surprisal values therefore cannot serve as the measure, and the version 1 results are reported for the record but not interpreted. The measurement code was correct, and the July numbers reproduce exactly. The frozen stimuli were rerun on Qwen3.8 27B, as a declared deviation from the registration. Neither the trigger prediction nor the post-region hypothesis holds (mean trigger contrast −0.48 bits, mean post contrast −0.27 bits, each positive in four of ten pairs). The reversed effect, its repetition mechanism and the calibration account of version 1 are withdrawn. This version adds the audit, the second-model run, the corrected pipeline description and the frozen design document; the stimuli, July data and July code are unchanged. Version 1 remains available. The study tested whether semantic reorganization, the “reveal” moment in which new information reframes previously read material, leaves a measurable trace in per-token surprisal when a language model reads short narrative texts. Ten matched stimulus pairs had byte-identical openings diverging into a reveal or a neutral continuation, and predictions were registered before any data collection. The successor measure registered in version 1, hidden-state distance on identical quoted-back text, is kept unchanged. A plain-language introduction to the measures is given in Bruyn (2026), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23360915. The null is reported in full, per the research program’s standing practice.

title: When Is a Temporal Statement Store a Statement Graph? Export Boundaries for Occurrence Records with Two Clocks
abstract: A temporal statement store keeps every occurrence of a statement as a record. Each record has its own identifier, a triple, a transaction-time lifetime and a valid-time interval, and other records can refer to it. This paper asks which part of such a store can be exported as a Statement Graph without inventing or renaming any occurrence. Statement Graphs are the DAG model behind OneGraph, which lets RDF-star and property graphs interoperate. A record set can be exported this way exactly when it is closed under references and acyclic. Every set contains a largest exportable subset, the export kernel. A linear-time topological peel computes it, and it can be kept up to date with one bit per record. If records are immutable and never deleted, the full history is closed. Exporting it then loses only the cycles that atomic corrections create, and a batch-local check at correction time prevents those as well. Exporting a single snapshot also drops supersession lineage. A dual reference closure keeps that lineage by adding the retracted records it points to. Every omitted record is reported with a reason. The exported history can be written into RDF-star with both clocks stored as reserved statements, and read back without loss. Conjunctive queries over the asserted part return the same answers, up to a quoting bijection. Two alternatives mark the boundary from either side:- RDF 1.2 reifiers export any store, cycles included, but assert per triple rather than per occurrence.- The property-graph branch admits only edges and properties that nothing references. The proofs in the paper are by hand. The validation archive adds:- a Lean 4 development that re-proves the main results;- an executable validator covering exhaustive small stores, random stores and random protocol histories;- traces of both counterexamples through the tiramemsu engine.

title: Governing Large Language Model Services for Confidential Microdata: A Decision Framework for National Statistical Offices
abstract: National statistical offices increasingly face requests to provide large language model (LLM) capabilities in secure research environments. The governance problem is to determine which service configurations, if any, can be supported safely on confidential microdata. These services challenge traditional statistical disclosure control because interaction is adaptive, systems may retrieve documents or call analytical tools, and outputs may appear plausible without being grounded in approved data. This paper proposes a governance framework that organizes each request as a sequence of decisions: whether an LLM is needed, which service mode is justified, which threat model applies, which controls are required, and what evidence must be reviewed before release. The framework spans deterministic pipelines, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-using agents, code-execution agents, linkage configurations, and fine-tuning.

title: Wendt's determinant and finiteness of prime characteristics for permutation binomials
abstract: For $f(X)=X^r(X^s+a)\in\mathbb F_{p^m}[X]$, with $m,r,s\geqslant1$ and $a\in\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$, put $g=\gcd(s,p^m-1)$. We prove that, for each fixed $g$, only finitely many prime characteristics $p$ admit such permutation binomials, even as $m,r,s,a$ vary. If $6\nmid g$, every such $p$ divides Wendt's determinant $W_g=\operatorname{Res}_X(X^g-1,(X+1)^g-1)$, which is nonzero. When $6\mid g$, this determinant vanishes; inverse power sums and iterated resultants yield an explicit nonzero integer divisible by every such $p>2g+1$. We determine the exact admissible characteristics for $1\leqslant g\leqslant10$, obtain a further divisibility condition over prime fields, and show that in prime fields $g=11$ occurs precisely when $p=23$.

title: CREATE: Creativity Evaluation of VLMs using the Visual Remote Associates Test
abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) are used in creative tasks such as visual storytelling, design ideation, art interpretation, and advertising. Yet we lack principled ways to measure the lateral reasoning of these models compared to human potential. We introduce CREATE, a semi-automatically constructed benchmark containing 155 visual Remote Associates Test problems. These problems require a solver to find an underlying connection among three seemingly dissimilar images. We conduct a human study (N=25) to validate and ground the quality of our benchmark, and evaluate 11 VLMs. Our findings show that most VLMs underperform humans on this task. Our experiments indicate that the associative ability of VLMs depends on the cue concepts provided in the text and does not universally extend to visual puzzles.

title: Over-parameterization Is Neither Robust nor Fragile in Matrix Sensing: A Geometric Theory of Solution Robustness
abstract: Over-parameterization is ubiquitous in modern machine learning, yet its effect on robustness remains poorly understood. We study this question in matrix sensing, a canonical non-convex problem that can also be viewed, under an appropriate parameterization, as training a two-layer quadratic neural network. We develop a rank-aware robustness theory for the Burer-Monteiro factorization when the search rank k may exceed the target rank r_star, thereby capturing over-parameterization. Our analysis shows that robustness depends jointly on the degree of over-parameterization and the local geometry of the attained second-order stationary point: increasing k generally worsens sensitivity, but stationary points with the same search rank can exhibit substantially different robustness. Motivated by this observation, we propose a trajectory-aware algorithm that uses spectral balancing and randomized sketching to steer optimization toward less sensitive solutions. In matrix-sensing experiments, the method reduces paired sensitivity by 18-29 percent for isotropic operators and 87-89 percent for weak-tail operators, without degrading reconstruction accuracy. These results demonstrate that parameter count alone does not determine robustness and identify solution geometry and the optimization trajectory as important levers for improving it.

title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
abstract: We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$. This leads to a correspondence with partial ovoids of the elliptic quadric $Q^-(5,q)$. Using a construction of Cossidente and Pavese, we obtain a non-additive symmetric $2$-code in $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ of cardinality $q^4+2q^3$, improving the previously known general lower bound. We also give an explicit matrix description of this family. Lastly, we present a block-based construction for symmetric $2$-codes that extends the three-dimensional improvement to all odd dimensions. In particular, for every odd $n\geq3$ and every prime power $q>2$, we obtain \begin{equation*} A_q^{\rm sym}(n,2) \ge q^{(n^2-1)/2}+q^{(n^2-3)/2}+q^{(n^2-9)/2}, \end{equation*} which is strictly larger than the maximum cardinality of an additive symmetric $2$-code with the same parameters. This yields the first infinite family (as the matrix dimension $n$ varies) of non-additive symmetric $2$-codes whose size is larger than the largest achievable size of an additive code with the same parameters; before this, such a gap had only been established for $n=3$.
