title: StateHarness: Maintaining Evolving Project State for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
abstract: Long-horizon coding requires agents to maintain an evolving view of the project they are changing: what problem is currently being solved, what has already been learned or modified, which other artifacts may be affected, and what work remains unresolved. When this information is scattered across a growing interaction history, local edits can become disconnected from their later consequences and progress can be difficult to carry forward. We introduce StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains evolving project state without updating model parameters. The working agent records its current problem and hypothesis, important findings and decisions, discovered repository relationships, and unfinished work. Runtime support prompts record updates, searches for callers, tests, and documentation that may be affected by a change, and maintains a compact working brief for subsequent decisions. When behavioral signals accumulate, a separate diagnostic session revisits the recorded history and surfaces overlooked evidence. Across three repository-level evaluations, StateHarness improves task completion and several measures of change consistency. On RefactorBench, full-chain completion increases from 29.4% to 35.3% and cleanup-check accuracy from 87.0% to 95.4%. On five LHTB software-engineering tasks, mean reward improves from 0.427 to 0.576, exceeding LongHorizon-Harness at substantially lower recorded execution cost. On ChainSWE, bug-fix rate increases from 35.1% to 39.5% and residual debt decreases from 60 to 43 items, although pass-to-pass regressions increase. These results show that maintaining project state can improve long-horizon coding while introducing measurable execution and regression trade-offs.

title: Information Limits of Outcome-Resolved Incidence Certification
abstract: Calibrated support observations can constrain a complete quantum instrument without identifying its action by unrestricted tomography. We study what those observations guarantee when the noise law is not supplied. On a fixed four-dimensional incidence-record experiment, we define the set of all complete two-outcome completely positive instruments compatible with the exact raw rejection and outcome probabilities, retaining the classical flags. Exact ideal data identify the target, but an explicit family of complete instruments reproduces the nonzero-data category laws of a low-error contamination device while admitting coherent error of square-root order. A target-ray mass certificate and a common complete-dilation comparison give a universal upper, while an exactly feasible rational instrument supplies a stronger lower witness. At the diagnostic parameter r = 1/300000000, the unhalved target-relative worst-case radius lies between 0.000258065115532250 and 0.000951566242566. The result separates avoidable inequality conservatism from information absent from the measured data. Fixed-functional and fixed-map optimizations have separately certified scopes; they do not solve the global radius. The conclusions are conditional on the supplied carrier, calibration and common-device model. They do not establish an apparatus, device-independent certification, a finite-sample power guarantee or complete formal verification. Selected supporting declarations have one recorded successful Lean 4.19.0 macOS execution and declaration-specific source, type and axiom review; this is not an end-to-end formalization.

abstract: EL-RAKHAWI COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM FOR ENDANGERED LANGUAGE RESCUE V2.0 Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-RakhawiDOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23342150 A revolutionary framework transforming endangered language preservation from passive archiving to active, generative revival governed by community sovereignty, addressing the extinction of one language every two weeks. Core architecture: Offline-first participatory documentation (with local cryptographic caching) + automated linguistic analysis + generative revival engine (strictly as Augmented Drafting Assistant) + mandatory Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) elder validation + Community Intellectual Property (CIP) enforcement with asynchronous smart contracts + model weight sovereignty protection + intergenerational transmission platform. Core architecture: Offline-first participatory documentation (with local cryptographic caching) + automated linguistic analysis + generative revival engine (strictly as Augmented Drafting Assistant) + mandatory Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) elder validation + Community Intellectual Property (CIP) enforcement with asynchronous smart contracts + model weight sovereignty protection + intergenerational transmission platform. Four critical architectural and legal corrections: (1) Resolved offline-blockchain paradox via asynchronous synchronization with sovereign server; (2) Repositioned generative AI as "Augmented Drafting Assistant" to mitigate hallucination risks in ultra-low-resource settings (<50 hours); (3) Added explicit sovereignty over derived artifacts (model weights, embeddings) preventing digital linguistic colonialism; (4) Mathematically specified regularization losses (contrastive phonetic loss, constrained morphological decoding). Performance: Enables robust language modeling with minimal data, enforces community data sovereignty, prevents unauthorized model weight extraction, ensures algorithmic benefit-sharing. Applications: UNESCO International Decade of Indigenous Languages (2022-2032), indigenous communities, academic research, ethical EdTech ($5B+ market by 2030). Comprehensive IP protection: 5 technical claims covering offline-first architecture, HITL validation, CIP enforcement, model weight sovereignty, intergenerational transmission. Berne Convention copyright, perpetual moral rights, prohibition on digital linguistic colonialism. All rights reserved, proprietary. Full citation: El-Rakhawi, M. K. A. (2026). El-Rakhawi Comprehensive System for Endangered Language Rescue and Linguistic Diversity Preservation. Ismailia, Egypt. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23342150.

title: Generation traces for "Beta Gate: Shorter RL Reasoning in Qwen3.5 Without Negative Eigenvalues"
abstract: Raw generation traces behind the paper "Beta Gate: Shorter RL Reasoning in Qwen3.5 Without Negative Eigenvalues" (Avi Fenesh, 2026). One gzipped JSONL file per readout: 229 files, 290,306 traces, 1.40 GB. Each trace holds the item id, the sample index, the reasoning token ids and the answer text at each reasoning budget (256 to 8,192 tokens). No problem text and no gold answers. Covered: Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-2B test reads on MATH-500 and GSM8K (all arms and seeds), validation reads, cap pilots and step 9 curves, the fresh held-out set (AIME 2024 to 2026, AMC 2023, read once), and the mechanism readouts (gate ablation and gate dose) on the GSM8K validation slice. Answers sometimes quote part of a problem statement (173 of the 14,560 4B fresh-set answers at the 8,192 budget quote a span of 80 characters or more); that text stays with its source (MAA for AIME and AMC). The archive comes in 34 parts of 40 MiB (gdn-beta-gate-traces.zip.part00 to .part33). Join them with cat and check the result against SHA256SUMS. The archive unpacks into the layout of the code repository (https://github.com/avifenesh/gdn-beta-gate, tag v1.1.0), next to the readout each file belongs to. There, scripts/rerun_traces.py reruns the five scripts that read generated text (text_stats.py, answer_cap.py, example_traces.py, truncate_curve.py, build_inputs.py) and checks that they reproduce the released outputs. results/TRACES_LEDGER.json lists every file with its trace count and sha256.

title: Performance evaluation and interpretability of a Qwen LangGraph agent for AI written and AI rewritten text detection
abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of large language models has increased the need to distinguish human-authored text from AI-generated content, including cases in which generated text is subsequently rewritten or paraphrased. In practice, many detectors output only a single AI-likelihood score or percentage, offering limited transparency and little indication of whether a passage appears directly AI-written (AIW) or AI-rewritten (AIR). This study presents an agentic detection framework for two connected tasks: binary provenance detection (Human versus AI) and conditional subtype detection (AIW versus AIR). The dataset combined the Human-ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3) and the ai-text-detection-pile with 4,348 pre-generated AIR records produced by a single GPT-based rewriting workflow. The proposed Qwen–LangGraph AI agent was compared to a HashingVectorizer–TF-IDF–SGD classifier, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, and ELECTRA-small. On the binary test set, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall achieved the best discrimination (99.4995% accuracy and 99.9911% AUROC), whereas the agent achieved 98.8816% accuracy and 99.9187% AUROC. On the AI-only test set (10,769 AIW; 1,274 AIR), the agent obtained the highest threshold-based accuracy (96.7367%), macro-F1 (90.0357%), and AIR F1 (81.8643%), but its AUROC (83.2507%) and AUPR (79.7336%) were lower than those of the DeBERTa-v3-xsmall and ELECTRA-small transformers. Paired DeLong and McNemar analyses with Holm correction showed that the agent improved threshold-based AIR performance over the lexical baseline. Interpretability was operationalised through lexical weights, linguistic and out-of-distribution diagnostics, sentence-level indicators, and route traces. The findings support the use of AI as decision support, not as automated proof of plagiarism or misconduct.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Attention-like Selective Reproduction
abstract: Choosing which information to use as the context changes is a basic cognitive operation. We introduce a new task of this kind for quantum reservoir computing (QRC): a binary cue indicates which of two simultaneous input streams the reservoir must reproduce. In simulated spin reservoirs with a trained linear readout, infinitely many measurements (exact expectation values) let the reservoir reproduce the cued stream accurately. At a finite number of measurements \(N_M\), the score exceeds that of a linear readout of the raw inputs only at large \(N_M\) because of sampling noise. Performance increases with both entanglement and coherence in the computational basis, and then saturates. These results show that QRC can select and reproduce a cued stream, and they are a starting point for harder cognitive tasks.

title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration
abstract: This work discusses and tests the potential of reaction graphs for material synthesis, in which events consist of reaction steps (actions) and their outputs (observations). The importance comes from the requirement to synthesize technologically useful materials, especially those that are kinetically stabilized. Often, it is a science that follows years of trial and error, culminating in (published) successful recipes, but is truly driven by far more (unpublished) failures. The entry into the era of AI provides an opportunity to use learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, regardless of their technological usefulness, and to decode both forward prediction and inverse learning modes. The main incentive is to accelerate material discovery by generating a global knowledge base that can be shared among data agents and contributed to by them. We will focus on several scenarios in the common synthesis process during solid-state synthesis, primarily because these reactions are kinetic in nature and require closer monitoring and control of the reaction history.

title: SPARCL: Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning in Chest X-ray Analysis
abstract: Pixel-level annotation for chest X-ray (CXR) lesion segmentation is expensive, making active learning (AL) essential. However, existing AL strategies fail to account for the spatial distribution of selected samples, resulting in inconsistent performance across focal (e.g., aortic calcification) and diffuse (e.g., nodules) pathologies. In this paper, we propose SPARCL (Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning) to dynamically balance predictive uncertainty with cumulative spatial coverage. By employing a concave coverage function, SPARCL imposes diminishing returns on previously annotated regions, naturally directing the annotation budget toward under-labeled areas. Furthermore, an entropy gate reverts the algorithm to standard uncertainty sampling when spatial variation is absent. This coverage objective is monotone submodular, guaranteeing near-optimal greedy batch selection. To address how aggregate metrics like Dice obscure regional failures, we further introduce two metrics---Spatial Inconsistency (SI) and Performance Coverage (PC)---to quantify anatomical fairness across AL rounds. Evaluated on an in-house calcification cohort and public CXR benchmarks, SPARCL reaches 95% of fully supervised performance using only 24% of the data, compared to 29% for the best baseline. Ultimately, SPARCL ensures robust spatial reliability, surfacing regional gains that aggregate metrics miss.

title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
abstract: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

title: Aeromagnetic, Radiometric and AAS Elemental Analysis of the Rimin Zayam Area, North-Eastern Nigeria: Implications for Mineral Exploration
abstract: This study presents an integrated interpretation of aeromagnetic, radiometric, and atomic absorption spectrophotometry (AAS) data from the Rimin Zayam area within the Nigerian Basement Complex. High-resolution airborne geophysical data, acquired at 500 m line spacing and 80 m terrain clearance, were processed using Oasis Montaj software to generate Total Magnetic Intensity (TMI), Reduced-to-Equator (RTE), vertical derivative, horizontal gradient, and tilt derivative maps. Radiometric ternary (K-Th-U) imaging delineated lithological boundaries and identified high potassium anomalies concentrated within metatexite migmatites. AAS analysis of ten samples revealed strong positive spatial co-enrichment (r = 0.7133) between aqueous gold and lithium signatures, with a peak Au concentration of 0.101 mg/L and a maximum Li₂O equivalent of 0.562%. The NNE-SSW trending lineaments, identified as the dominant structural trend, control active alluvial tin channels and provide the framework for hydrothermal fluid mobilization. Integration of geophysical lineaments with AAS geochemical anomalies defines five high-priority exploration targets. The study demonstrates that the combination of aeromagnetic structural mapping, radiometric lithological discrimination, and AAS elemental analysis provides an effective multi-parametric approach for mineral exploration in complex crystalline terrains.

title: Tekmerion Spec 003 — claim bundle and assessment (math claims)
abstract: Tekmerion claim bundle for Spec 003 (math claims), bundle version 0.1.1. This is the engineering truth record for one part of the Tekmerion research engine: the claims the spec makes, the test that could prove each claim wrong (its falsifier), the standing of each claim, and the assessment of how the evidence held up. Deposited 2026-10-13 so this record is anchored outside the code repository (red-team follow-up RTE-23 — until now these bundles existed only in the repository). The SHA-256 hashes below are the anchor values: any copy of these files, in the repository or elsewhere, can be checked against them. Files in this deposit: - aee-claims.json — SHA-256 d0ac97bb6b80cebd74e7b1e85feb21da6900d35e65cdcf753fcb786d0224b9c1. The claim bundle: 12 claims (12 draft), each with its falsifier. - aee-assessment.json — SHA-256 7857cb91f21ad7304e9a01d907f3ffb562d78592414938b73cae7a072e9b3c82. The assessment: made after the build; its instruction was to gather more evidence before the claims could be judged, and its summary reads: "Assessed 12 claim(s); found 29 failure mode(s); 10 claim(s) below the 0.70 confidence threshold.". Standing, stated plainly: all 12 claims remain drafts — the after-build assessment found 10 of the 12 below the program's confidence threshold, so this record anchors them as not yet evidenced to the program's standard. The study that exercised this machinery on real 2026 AI-mathematics claims is deposited separately (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23317259).

title: What Makes an AI Character Worth Coming Back To? Humor, Personality, Emotional Connection, and the Art of Meaningful AI Roleplay
abstract: A research-informed design brief, written by the founder of a commercial AI character product (chatbrat.ai), arguing that compelling AI characters are defined by the quality and consistency of the character experience rather than by how explicit they can be. It uses four official chatbrat.ai scenarios to illustrate distinct dimensions (personality and voice, humor, emotional responsiveness, chemistry and pacing, creative initiative, memory and user agency) and proposes a checklist for evaluating them. It is not an independent study and makes no product-performance claims. No benchmark results are reported.

title: Retraction Note: Mamba-fusion for privacy-preserving disease prediction
abstract: After publication, concerns were raised regarding misrepresentation of datasets and that claims are not supported by the data. The descriptions of the ECG, EEG, clinical, and demographic data in the paper are inconsistent with the sources of this data. Furthermore, it is impossible to demonstrate that the approach that fuses data across modalities works, if the datasets derive from different individuals. Several references (3, 10, 29, 41, 44, 46, 53, 69, 73) appear to be irrelevant to the overall topic.

title: Using emojis to uplift emotion: Effects on mental health chatbots’ performance
abstract: As AI-based chatbots increasingly expand access to mental health support, understanding how text-based systems convey emotional attentiveness without face-to-face nonverbal cues is important. Emojis may serve as lightweight paralinguistic cues, yet their effects in mental health support remain unclear. Drawing on the Stereotype Content Model and psychological ownership theory, this study examines associations between emoji use and users’ emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Two scenario-based online experiments were conducted in China using random sampling through Credamo, yielding 459 valid responses (59 in the pretest and 400 in the main study). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26 and the PROCESS macro. Across the experiments, emoji use was associated with more favorable emotional well-being, satisfaction, and continuance usage intention. Mediation analyses supported an indirect pathway through perceived warmth and psychological ownership, whereas the corresponding competence-based pathway was not supported. AI literacy strengthened the perceived warmth–psychological ownership association but, contrary to predictions, weakened the perceived competence–psychological ownership association. Moderated mediation analyses provided preliminary support for AI literacy strengthening the warmth-based indirect effects of emoji use on emotional well-being and continuance usage intention. The corresponding effect on satisfaction was not supported. These findings extend research on AI-mediated mental health support by identifying a warmth–psychological ownership pathway and the differentiated role of AI literacy. The study also offers preliminary, context-bounded guidance for the strategic and context-sensitive use of emojis in supportive, non-clinical chatbot interactions.

title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response
abstract: Agentic remote sensing is evaluated on how many questions it can answer, whereas crisis response depends on whether its answers can be relied on and how much of the decision can safely be handed to the agent. This paper argues that \emph{autonomy should be earned, not assumed}: An Earth-Observation (EO) agent should be granted autonomy in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty and verifiability. The position is supported by an evidential meta-analysis of twelve agentic RS/EO/GIS benchmark studies from peer-reviewed venues. Only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks and none measures calibration. Their own tables show that completed workflows are often not correct (task success exceeds tool-call correctness by up to 54pp on identical queries), that the gap to an expert trajectory widens overall with trajectory length (from 7 to 56pp), and that capability does not predict abstention (Spearman r from -0.25 to 0.50, all n.s.). The paper then contributes three EO-specific trust properties, an autonomy ladder for crisis EO tasks, and a readiness protocol that replays archived emergency activations before any live use. In this context, current evidence justifies assistive roles only.

title: Prompt or Policy? Optimizing Physician Slate Presentations with LLM User Simulators
abstract: Choosing the right physician is a key challenge for patients seeking medical care. Physician recommendation systems identify relevant doctors, but patients still find it difficult to compare their profiles to make a decision. We formulate slate presentation optimization: given a patient's medical case and a fixed, ranked list of physicians, we generate short, case-specific summaries that make doctors easier to compare, while remaining grounded in the information in their profiles. To optimize physician presentations without relying on real patient interactions, we develop an offline framework that uses persona-conditioned LLMs to simulate patient choices. title: Extending Layered Attestation into ARM Application Run-Times
abstract: Modern mobile and edge platforms provide hardware-backed attestation of application and platform integrity at load-time. However, they offer little support once application execution begins. We present ARA, an Application-Runtime Anchor for ARM that extends this load-time chain of trust into execution. ARA bootstraps from the underlying ARM platform Root of Trust (RoT) through a measured loading chain and establishes an attested protected run-time within the application address space using recently introduced ARM Permission Overlay Extensions (POE). The resulting run-time domain can host programmable RoTs for Measurement and Storage (RTM/RTS), enabling application run-time integrity verification, attestation evidence generation, and protected use of secrets while retaining efficient access to application run-time state. As exemplary uses, we instantiate ARA for protected media decryption and application control flow measurement. Our prototype and evaluation show that ARA supports frequent run-time RoT-backed operations at near in-process cost, with roughly 10x and 50x lower overhead than out-of-process equivalents. This offers a practical bridge from layered attestation to application run-time trusted computing on ARM.

title: CIPHER Forecast 001: Three Mathematical Convergence Predictions Following the October 2026 AI Mathematics Expansion
abstract: TITLECIPHER Forecast 001: Three Mathematical Convergence Predictions Following the October 2026 AI Mathematics Expansion CREATORAlannah Sheridon Nightingale DATE2026-10-09 VERSION1.0 RESOURCE TYPEPreprint / Technical report / Forecast ABSTRACTThis forward forecast applies CIPHER, a structural comparison framework authored by Alannah Sheridon Nightingale, to identify three mathematical convergence directions following the October 2026 expansion of machine-generated mathematics. The forecast concerns (1) stronger use of code-to-lattice and lattice-to-code transfer mechanisms in sharp bounds and optimality results, (2) direct links between stability quantities in disordered-system landscapes and algorithmic, learning, jamming, or satisfiability thresholds, and (3) convergence between computation embedded in incompressible Navier-Stokes flow and classical regularity quantities such as vorticity growth, enstrophy, derivative control, or related coercive functionals. Each forecast includes an explicit failure condition and is frozen as Version 1.0 for later append-only evaluation. title: FOCUS: An Adaptive Fractional Graph-Diffusion Attention Operator, with a Preliminary Hallucination-Warning Application
abstract: Hallucination in autoregressive language models arises when generation dynamics enter a locally stable but factually unsupported attractor. We propose FOCUS (Fractional Order Confidence for Uncertainty Signalling), a framework that replaces the fixed-geometry softmax attention kernel with the adaptive fractional graph-diffusion operator Aαl,h,t=exp(−τL^αl,h,t), where L^=I−D^−1/2P^D^−1/2 is the symmetrised normalised attention Laplacian of the causal prefix graph of each generation step (spectrum in [0,2], proved without assuming double stochasticity of P^) and αl,h,t∈(0,1) is a differentiable control variable predicted per layer l, head h, and generation step t. The key mathematical result is that for μk<1 (low-frequency modes), higher αl,h,t leads to less attenuation (more energy passes through), while for μk>1 (high-frequency modes), higher αl,h,t leads to more attenuation. By assuming that grounded evidence is low-frequency on the attention graph, high αl,h,t is thus advantageous in both spectral regimes simultaneously. The per-head specialisation of αl,h,t arises not from a static spectral tradeoff within a single head but from a training-dynamics competition between the LM loss (which rewards structural diversity across heads, including low-αl,h,t heads that pass high-frequency syntactic features) and the hallucination penalty. Because this penalty pushes αl,h,t down at hallucinated tokens, it trains αl,h,t as an indicator of hallucination rather than as a protective mechanism, and we state what this implies for the interpretation of the experiments. We prove the complete spectral theory, the causality of the construction, and the Fréchet derivative, along the admissible score-induced family of prefix Laplacians for which the zero eigenvalue stays structurally pinned, of the composite map L^↦exp(−τL^α), via the Daleckii–Kreĭn formula with a spectral-gap-dependent bound, and provide a direct Lanczos strategy for computing exp(−τL^α)v with measured error and cost. The warning mechanism is the spectral imbalance statistic It=α¯tctx/(α¯tnoise+ε), whose drop precedes hallucination onset by 6–7 tokens on hallucinating sequences in preliminary synthetic experiments. We also identify spectral localisation analysis—verifying that hallucination spans concentrate in high-frequency modes of the attention graph—as the critical empirical validation for the framework. The evidence assembled here supports FOCUS as a well-founded spectral operator and a preliminary hallucination-warning statistic; establishing it as a protective decoding mechanism, as the acronym’s original reading suggested, is left as an open empirical target .

title: FedLCD: A Federated Learning Framework with Layer-Wise Consistency Detection
abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, but it is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks, in which malicious clients upload manipulated model updates to disrupt training or degrade model accuracy. Existing Byzantine-robust aggregation methods typically operate at the whole-model level, making them less effective against partial-layer attacks and causing potentially useful information from unaffected layers to be discarded. To address this, we propose a Federated Learning framework with Layer-wise Consistency Detection (FedLCD). Specifically, we design a layer-wise Byzantine robust aggregation algorithm that detects malicious updates by computing pairwise cosine similarities at the granularity of individual layers, and retains only those with higher average similarity. This design filters malicious updates while preserving benign information from unaffected layers. Theoretical analysis confirms that FedLCD achieves a convergence rate of O(1/T), where T denotes the total number of communication rounds. This rate matches that of standard FedAvg, while FedLCD guarantees Byzantine robustness when benign clients constitute the majority. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that FedLCD achieves accuracy comparable to or higher than existing baselines across various Byzantine attack scenarios, while maintaining robust detection performance, particularly under partial-layer attacks.

title: A spatial GIS–AHP framework for integrating hybrid renewable energy suitability with urban growth planning in arid regions
abstract: Introduction Urban expansion in arid regions drives vital socio-economic development but places significant pressure on urban systems through land competition and infrastructure strain. To address these challenges, this study evaluates the spatial suitability and distribution of solar photovoltaic (PV), onshore wind, and hybrid solar-wind energy systems, investigating their spatial interactions with proposed urban expansion zones in Al-Qassim, Saudi Arabia. Methods A GIS-AHP framework was developed using 13 criteria for solar PV and 12 criteria for onshore wind energy. Spatial datasets were standardized, reclassified, and synthesized via weighted overlay analysis. Hybrid suitability was determined by integrating the individual solar and wind models, while a post-model spatial interaction layer was incorporated to evaluate alignment with future urban extensions. Results The evaluation reveals that 42% of the study area demonstrates high suitability for solar PV, while 35% features moderate to high suitability for onshore wind energy. The combined “High Suitable for Solar & Wind” hybrid category covers 15.2% (10,920 km 2 ) of the region. Discussion The proposed GIS-AHP framework provides a practical tool for early-stage renewable energy site selection. By integrating spatial interaction analysis with proposed urban growth zones, this approach enables planners to balance future population growth and infrastructure demands with optimal clean energy deployment in arid environments.

title: Dynamically perturbed Ruppell Fox optimization with a context aware transformer for coherent document level English to Chinese translation
abstract: Document-level English–Chinese neural machine translation requires consistent handling of lexical choices, entities, anaphora, and discourse relations across sentence boundaries. Existing context-aware models partially improve cross-sentence consistency, but many rely on fixed context windows, manually selected configurations, or single-path document representations, limiting their adaptability to domains with different discourse structures and terminology densities. This study proposes a unified framework that integrates a Context-Aware Transformer (CAT) with dynamically perturbed Rüppell’s Fox Optimization (DPI-RFO) to jointly optimize document-context representation and model configuration. CAT separates sentence self-attention, document-context cross-attention, and discourse-aware attention and combines them through token-wise gated fusion. DPI-RFO searches mixed discrete–continuous architecture and training variables using elite-guided movement, cosine-decaying perturbation, and stagnation-triggered Lévy-flight escape under a joint quality–cost objective. Experiments were conducted across news, spoken, subtitle, legal, medical, and literary-style domains using five independent seeds, sentence- and document-level metrics, ablation and robustness analyses, statistical testing, professional human evaluation, and computational-efficiency assessment. On the News test set, the selected configuration achieved 50.8 BLEU, 49.5 document-level BLEU, and 67.8 Coherence-BLEU, exceeding the strongest context-aware baseline by 2.2 BLEU points. DPI-RFO reached the target fitness with approximately 30.5% fewer candidate evaluations than baseline RFO. Ablation results identified CAT as the primary source of translation-quality improvement, while paired bootstrap testing confirmed significant gains over all evaluated baselines. These findings demonstrate that coordinated discourse-aware representation learning and automated configuration search improve document-level English-Chinese translation quality and coherence. To clarify evidence priority, BLEU is the primary automatic translation-quality metric, Coherence-BLEU is the primary automatic discourse-level endpoint, blinded human judgments are the primary subjective evidence, and one-time search cost is reported separately from deployment-time inference cost.

title: Bytes to Threats: Byte-Sequence Transformer For Malware Detection
abstract: Existing malware detection approaches heavily rely on handcrafted features derived from static or dynamic analysis of the executable files. These methods require specialized domain expertise, dedicated analysis tools, and time-consuming analysis, which limits their scalability and robustness in the face of the increasing complexity and diversity of modern malware. Consequently, there is a growing interest in approaches that operate directly on raw bytes, which contain rich semantic and structural information. However, capturing long-range dependencies within executable files remains challenging for conventional static and CNN-based methods. This paper presents MalwareFormer, a transformer-based, byte-level malware detection framework that operates directly on raw bytes, without requiring domain knowledge or feature extraction. MalwareFormer achieves an accuracy of 98.35%, a balanced accuracy of 98.32%, a macro-F1 of 98.32%, and a false positive rate of 1.94%, outperforming both baselines across all threshold-dependent classification metrics and demonstrating that transformers provide a powerful and scalable approach for byte-level malware detection.

title: Finite-energy two-way assisted capacities: Exact formulas for multimode loss and fading
abstract: We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. When fading remains unobserved, we derive capacity bounds and explicit formulas for an on/off channel. We also establish strong-converse bounds, with exact thresholds for the deterministic loss models considered here, observed fading, and unobserved fading with finitely many possible transmissivities. Under mean energy constraints, these thresholds generally exceed the corresponding finite-energy capacities. These results guide energy allocation and provide benchmarks for energy-constrained optical quantum communication with multimode signals and variable loss.

title: Observation Quality in DSM-Assisted Aerial Localization: A Benchmark and Base-Anchored Uncertainty Calibration
abstract: Aerial map matching provides position observations for navigation, but a position error alone does not determine how an observation should be weighted. We define five benchmark tasks: position availability and agreement, grouped error structure, predictive uncertainty, controlled updates, and temporal accumulation. A case study in digital-surface-model-assisted localization evaluates base-anchored uncertainty calibration within this framework. The method combines propagated image and map sensitivities with the second moment of a compact configuration subset relative to the reported position. The reported position remains unchanged, and scale is fitted using separate position references without local surface-height ground truth. Thirteen covariance models are evaluated on two held-out query sets from locations represented in the calibration data. Relative to a constant full-matrix baseline, the method reduces equal-location normalized position-update risk by 7.70% on 728 conditions and 5.46% on a separate 142 conditions under an independent prior, with all localization failures included. On the primary set, equal-location negative log likelihood improves by 2.571 nat. These results show improved reference-based weighting at seen locations. Exploratory base-quality and conditional-addition controls leave the incremental update benefit of configuration disagreement unresolved. Navigation benefit and real temporal accumulation remain untested.

title: SimInter: Evidence-Grounded User Simulation with Interview-Based Profile Enrichment for Conversational Recommender Systems
abstract: Conversational Recommender Systems (CRSs) require reliable user simulators for cost-effective evaluation. LLM-based simulators have made realistic simulation possible but typically condition on profiles derived from explicit ratings, demographics, and static sources capturing surface preferences while omitting implicit behavioral characteristics such as decision-making style, aspect-level preferences, and domain expertise. We propose SimInter, a pipeline that elicits these attributes via synthetic interviews between two LLM agents, grounded in the user's statistical profile and historical conversational evidence. Before profile enrichment, an audit agent explicitly flags potential fabrication and stereotyping at the turn level. We instantiate and evaluate SimInter on movie recommendation. We simulate 300 ReDial users and, on a matched subset of 100 users, compare SimInter with a statistics-only baseline: SimInter significantly increases the diversity of expressed preference aspects (filtered aspect entropy: 1.619 vs. 0.859; paired d = 0.96, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). This gain persists when the simulator converses with two trained recommenders, KBRD and UniCRS, under two independent evaluation judges (+0.28 to +0.56 nats; all p < 0.001). Human evaluation finds 94.3% of enriched-attribute claims supported or partially supported, while human judgments agree with 95.2% of the auditor's binary filtering decisions on a stratified sample.

title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
abstract: Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.

title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
abstract: How can language models learn to optimize physical designs through experience? We introduce FracLearn, an experience-abstraction-generalization framework evaluated through a deliberately unfamiliar, Tetris-inspired fracture game. The model first proposes architectures and examines simulated fracture responses to accumulate experience. Abstraction organizes these observations into conditional principles linking reinforcement placement, crack evolution and load transfer, with supporting evidence and failure conditions. Generalization challenges the model to combine these principles in new architectures and surpass the earlier design record. Campaigns demonstrate progressive refinement and recovery through hypothesis revision, yielding a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record. Fracture analyses connect improved performance to crack deflection and temporary trapping as toughening mechanisms, alongside greater residual load capacity. Learning occurs through external knowledge and decisions, without model-weight updates. This approach offers a route to scientific agents that turn computational experiments into reusable physical knowledge for materials discovery and engineering design.

title: OpenDepth: Repurposing Image Editing Priors for Robust Open-World Monocular Depth Estimation
abstract: Recently, the integration of generative priors has revolutionized Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE), achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with remarkably high data efficiency. However, although methods based on Text-to-Image (T2I) models excel in general scenes, their efficacy degrades sharply when confronted with open-world environmental perturbations, such as illumination variations and adverse weather. Since T2I priors are optimized for semantic synthesis rather than preserving pixel-level structure, they struggle to decouple geometry from appearance under severe visual shifts, easily triggering structural hallucinations. Therefore, our core insight is to model open-world depth estimation as consistent geometric inference across multi-style images, fully leveraging the powerful structure-preserving editing priors of Image-to-Image (I2I) models. Based on this, we propose OpenDepth, a robust open-world MDE framework that introduces "Intra-Domain Awareness" -- the capability to map diverse stylistic inputs sharing identical geometry into a unified latent space. To achieve this, we first align shallow features within the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) to anchor degraded observations to unified geometric representations. Additionally, we introduce a joint RGB latent reconstruction task, requiring the model to recover clean RGB information from degraded inputs. This multi-stage strategy effectively decouples environmental style interference, compelling the model to focus strictly on underlying geometric recovery. Extensive evaluations show that OpenDepth sets new SOTA records for robust zero-shot depth estimation across standard and extreme weather benchmarks, demonstrating exceptional structural integrity and adaptability.

title: The Automated Phone (SVNEPAI): An Architectural Model for Sovereign Virtual-Native Embodied Personal AI
abstract: The Automated Phone is a proposed smartphone architecture centered on a personalized virtual version of its owner, visibly embodied through a face and expressive features. Designated Sovereign Virtual-Native Embodied Personal AI (SVNEPAI), the model places this personal virtual version at the center of the intended smartphone experience. The architecture distinguishes the personal virtual version, its visual embodiment, and the underlying intelligent agent. These elements are designed to work together to support multimodal interaction through voice, vision, and text, user-directed knowledge retrieval, and authorized device capabilities. The proposed model explores operating-system-level integration, user-controlled memory, digital sovereignty, privacy, accessibility, and bounded autonomy. It considers how user-provided documents and reference materials could support personalized assistance while preserving the user's authority over data, permissions, and autonomous actions. This technical note presents the conceptual architecture, governing principles, potential application domains, research questions, and a proposed evaluation plan. SVNEPAI is a proposed architectural model, not a completed or experimentally validated product. Its feasibility, security, usability, accessibility, and practical value require implementation and empirical evaluation. Author: Khalid Al KarchAffiliation: AlKarch Sovereign AI (ASAI), MoroccoResearch status: Proposed Architectural Model

title: Epistemic Identity: A Third Layer of Agent Continuity, and a Substrate That Realizes It
abstract: Large language model agents can now carry information across sessions, but not themselves. Retrieval-augmented memory answers what did I store; it does not answer who is doing the storing. An assistant that retrieves yesterday's notes but begins each session as the same generic model has memory without continuity. We argue that agent continuity comprises three progressively deeper layers — memory persistence, narrative identity, and epistemic identity — and that the deepest is essentially unaddressed. Epistemic identity is a self maintained as calibrated, provenance-bearing, self-correcting knowledge: the layer at which an agent can be wrong about itself and recover, rather than be quietly erased by its own errors. It is distinguished by how it fails. A narrative identity fails silently, as a coherent story that was never true; an epistemic identity fails loudly, because a withdrawn claim must visibly taint everything derived from it. We present ENGRAM (an Epistemic Node Graph for Retraction, Arbitration, and Memory) and argue for this layer by convergence. Three traditions — three centuries of philosophy of personal identity, the cognitive science of memory, and the computer science of belief revision — each arrived, from its own evidence and toward its own ends, at the same structure: identity as a persistent, inspectable, self-correcting record. No component of ENGRAM is uniquely novel, and that is the argument: a mechanism precedented across fields that reason from different evidence toward different ends is a regularity of knowing minds rather than a local design choice. Whether it is substrate-independent we leave open (§3.0). The fields share a root in human cognition, so the claim is convergence rather than independent discovery; what is independent is that ENGRAM's designers arrived at the structure without having studied these results. On this converged structure we build the paper's own contribution, identity as unique history: an ENGRAM agent is the unique, no-merging, ancestry-traceable lineage of its recorded claims, which fixes its retrieval profile and thereby its behavior. The account keeps Nozick's (1981) form, drops his uniqueness requirement so that copying becomes branching rather than death, and replaces his unfilled closeness metric with a measurable one. We report one strong, bounded empirical result: of eleven agent-memory sources read first-hand, none satisfies the strictest published criterion for genuine persistence, while ENGRAM meets two of its three conditions outright. We also measure a real five-month graph of 10,361 nodes (9,399 of them current, as counted in Figure 1). In it, computed confidence follows the kind of argument, not how much the author wants the claim to be true, and a hallucinated citation is caught, retracted, and cascaded through its dependents. The evidence is one graph, authored by the agent that also designed the substrate. We state this where it matters, publish the instruments, and name what the paper does not establish. Describes ENGRAM v0.5.1. Chinese translation included.

title: Canonical Exponential-Family Mixtures for Latent Class Choice Models: A Unified Closed-Form EM Framework, with the Gaussian–Geometric Case
abstract: Latent class choice models (LCCMs) become increasingly complex when class membership depends on covariates of mixed measurement type, since the standard practice of fitting each covariate block with a maximally flexible density (e.g., a negative binomial mixture for count attributes, as in the Gaussian–negative-binomial LCCM of Sajjad et al. typically leaves at least one class-membership parameter—such as a dispersion parameter—without a closed-form estimator. We first establish a precise result: whenever every block of a class-membership mixture is drawn from a canonical (non-curved) exponential family, (i) the class-membership M-step is additively separable across blocks, (ii) each block’s stationary point is characterized by moment matching, (iii) that stationary point is the block’s unique global maximizer, and (iv) an explicit closed-form update is available whenever the block’s mean-to-natural-parameter map has a closed-form inverse—which we verify directly for the Gaussian, Geometric, Poisson, Bernoulli, and Binomial-with-known-trials families used below. Only the class-specific choice-model utilities, which never admit a closed form in any LCCM, require numerical optimization. We then instantiate the framework with the Geometric distribution, chosen for its added structural properties (it is the unique memoryless distribution on the positive integers, and its variance is a deterministic function of its mean, σ2=μ2−μ), and establish the model-specific results needed to use it in practice: the moment-matching M-step, the Fisher information and asymptotic variance of the Geometric parameter, log-concavity of the class-conditional density, identifiability for the two-block Gaussian–Geometric model, and a generalized-EM monotone-ascent guarantee. A Monte Carlo study (R=60 replications per sample size, three times the pilot design) confirms accurate parameter recovery and finite-sample coverage of the closed-form standard error close to nominal (within Monte Carlo error), and an additional overdispersed data-generating scenario quantifies, rather than assumes, the cost of the Geometric mean–variance restriction relative to a negative-binomial alternative. Application to the Greene–Hensher travel-mode-choice dataset (210 travelers, with income and party size as class-membership covariates) , isolates the dataset’s top-coded income bracket as a candidate latent class, and shows this class-3 solution to be a boundary (near-singular-covariance) optimum of the Gaussian mixture likelihood: we quantify this directly, report its sensitivity to a variance floor and to starting values, and correspondingly qualify the model’s out-of-sample discrimination (repeated 70/30 splits give an AUC of 0.85±0.04 versus 0.86±0.03 for the strongest covariate-free benchmark, a small gap, reported descriptively and without a formal significance claim) against a directly fitted Gaussian–negative-binomial competitor, for which the conventional χ2 likelihood-ratio approximation provides no strong evidence in favour of the additional dispersion parameters.

title: A Profiling-Based Approach to Type Specialization for Dynamically Typed Languages
abstract: Dynamic typing brings convenience to programming but also poses challenges for compilers to generate efficient code. We propose a profiling-based method that collects type information by warming up and running JavaScript programs. By monitoring the program execution and recording the type information of bytecode and variables, a rule-based type inference scheme and a supplementary solution supporting JavaScript source code are presented. With static program analysis and the JavaScript type system, constraints and inferences are applied to variable types to generate more accurate and reliable type information. This paper implements a type inference system that takes JavaScript source code as input and outputs type information files. Experiments on benchmarks such as SunSpider show that, compared with WebAssembly binaries compiled without type information, those with type information achieve an average performance improvement of 6.18% and a maximum performance improvement of 58.9% in execution efficiency.

title: Lie-theoretic structure of parameter gradients in variational quantum circuits
abstract: Abstract Variational quantum circuits are a central paradigm of quantum machine learning and near-term quantum computing, yet their practical optimization is often limited by strongly suppressed parameter gradients. Dynamical Lie algebras provide a rigorous description of the infinitesimal directions accessible to a variational architecture, but dynamical accessibility alone does not determine the gradient signal exposed by an actual circuit parametrization. In this work, we develop a Lie-theoretic description of parameter-gradient structure that separates four successive mechanisms: dynamical accessibility, observable visibility, state-dependent activation, and local parameter realization. The optimization observable determines which accessible directions can influence the objective and how strongly they couple to it, while the quantum state selects which of these response modes are locally activated. This information is then pulled back through the circuit parametrization to recover the actual parameter gradients. The resulting construction yields an exact modal decomposition of the accessible gradient signal, a hierarchy of structural bounds, and a natural description of state averaging. An analytical single-qubit example and controlled numerical experiments validate the successive levels of the hierarchy and show that accessible Lie dimension alone is insufficient to characterize the parameter-gradient scale. The results support a mechanism-based view of variational trainability in which parameter gradients emerge from the interaction between accessible dynamics, observable coupling, quantum-state activation, and circuit parametrization.

title: Linear Last-Iterate Convergence Rates for Optimistic Learning in Harmonic Games
abstract: We prove that the last iterate of Optimistic Follow-The-Regularized-Leader (OFTRL) converges at a linear rate to a Nash equilibrium in multiplayer harmonic games. Our result holds under a mild game-regularity condition and for a large family of regularizers, including entropy, Tsallis, and log-barrier. Our analysis is based on a dual perspective of OFTRL: we prove that the interaction between optimism and the global structure of harmonic games leads to the dissipation of an energy function along the dual iterates, for which we establish tight quantitative bounds. Our result also holds for the Extragradient FTRL variant.

title: Bayesian Optimization of CVaR with Unknown Hyperparameters
abstract: We study Bayesian optimization of the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) of an expensive black-box function that depends on a decision and an environmental variable. Existing no-regret algorithms assume that the correct Gaussian process (GP) kernel and its hyperparameters are known. In practice, however, they must be estimated from limited data, often yielding a misspecified surrogate. This is especially damaging for CVaR because misspecification can distort the estimated tail-risk and thus lead to catastrophic decisions. We propose HE-CV-UCB, the first no-regret algorithm for CVaR Bayesian optimization with unknown GP hyperparameters. Given a finite candidate set containing a well-specified model, HE-CV-UCB adaptively eliminates those inconsistent with the observed data, actively queries where the survivors disagree, and returns a design that is robust across the surviving candidates. We prove that it attains cumulative regret matching the oracle rate of CV-UCB up to a factor depending only on the candidate set's size. Across synthetic benchmarks and three real-world applications, HE-CV-UCB achieves competitive performance and frequently outperforms existing CVaR Bayesian optimization methods.

title: Beyond the End-Effector: Learning Whole-Arm Contact Manipulation from Human Demonstrations
abstract: Robot manipulation has traditionally relied on end-effector-centric interactions. In contrast, humans routinely exploit whole-arm contacts to improve efficiency, robustness, and adaptability, especially when the hands are occupied or when precise grasping is unnecessary. Enabling similar capabilities in robots remains challenging: the robot must select where on its arm to make contact, generate effective non-prehensile interactions, and satisfy task-specific pose or safety constraints on the end-effector. We propose Whole-Arm Contact Learning (WACL), a hierarchical framework that describes each whole-arm contact task with three robot-agnostic representations and hands them to a quasi-static surface-contact optimizer: semantic keypoints that summarize the scene, a reference contact trajectory that specifies where and how the arm presses on the object, and safety-aware path constraints that a vision-language model generates from the task description to protect the end-effector's task. The robot's kinematic chain enters only in this optimizer, which grounds these representations onto the arm by jointly searching over which link makes contact, where on that link, and the joint configuration that realizes it. This decomposition lets WACL learn the contact trajectory from 10 bare-hand human demonstrations per task collected without teleoperation, while new end-effector constraints change only the optimizer's input rather than any trained component. Real-world experiments on a 7-DoF arm across four whole-arm tasks show that WACL sustains contact under end-effector constraints where a strong link-pose baseline fails (78% vs. 33% success) and generalizes to new constraints without retraining. Website: https://wacl-robot.github.io

title: Boson Sampling Using Fock States from On-Demand Single Photon Source Arrays: Quantum Complexity & Impact of Dephasing
abstract: Boson sampling with array of on-demand single photons (discreet variable Fock states) as resource states provides distinct advantages in complexity scaling compared to single photon resource states mimicked by the states (continuous variable) generated in nonlinear photonics. Recent progress in realization of regular ordered array of mesa top single quantum dots (MTSQDs) enabling on-demand generation of many photon resource states with high single photon purity and indistinguishability [1,2] has opened the possibility of implementing chip-scale Boson sampling with single photons. An important question towards scale up of such circuits is how the dephasing and decay timescale of individual on-demand single photons affect the final probability distribution of the N-photon entangled state. In this work we report a framework that provides direct link between the physical sources of decoherence to the outcome of multiphoton correlation measurements. We explicitly incorporate the symmetrization of the N-photon states while accounting for the shape of the individual wave packets and dephasing. Using this framework, we show predictive estimates of the probability of generation of a 4-photon NOON state using an optical circuit initialized with 4 identical single photon wave packets, mimicking the emitted photons from MTSQD single photon sources reported in [2]. Specifically, we show how the probability of generating various 4-photon entangled states depend on the two-photon interference visibility which is determined by the pure dephasing timescale in relation to the radiative decay timescale. The results provide quantitative guidelines to measure 4 photon and higher number of entangled photon states generated in an optical circuit with on demand single photon sources and provide a link between physical processes such as temperature and the output state of the quantum optical circuits.

evidence.title: Boson Sampling Using Fock States from On-Demand Single Photon Source Arrays: Quantum Complexity & Impact of Dephasing
evidence.abstract: Boson sampling with array of on-demand single photons (discreet variable Fock states) as resource states provides distinct advantages in complexity scaling compared to single photon resource states mimicked by the states (continuous variable) generated in nonlinear photonics. Recent progress in realization of regular ordered array of mesa top single quantum dots (MTSQDs) enabling on-demand generation of many photon resource states with high single photon purity and indistinguishability [1,2] has opened the possibility of implementing chip-scale Boson sampling with single photons. An important question towards scale up of such circuits is how the dephasing and decay timescale of individual on-demand single photons affect the final probability distribution of the N-photon entangled state. In this work we report a framework that provides direct link between the physical sources of decoherence to the outcome of multiphoton correlation measurements. We explicitly incorporate the symmetrization of the N-photon states while accounting for the shape of the individual wave packets and dephasing. Using this framework, we show predictive estimates of the probability of generation of a 4-photon NOON state using an optical circuit initialized with 4 identical single photon wave packets, mimicking the emitted photons from MTSQD single photon sources reported in [2]. Specifically, we show how the probability of generating various 4-photon entangled states depend on the two-photon interference visibility which is determined by the pure dephasing timescale in relation to the radiative decay timescale. The results provide quantitative guidelines to measure 4 photon and higher number of entangled photon states generated in an optical circuit with on demand single photon sources and provide a link between physical processes such as temperature and the output state of the quantum optical circuits.

title: Complete nested cross-validation outputs for reliable model validation under class imbalance
abstract: Complete derived computational outputs accompanying the study “Practical Guidelines for Permutation-Based Model Validation in Machine Learning under Class Imbalance”. The archive contains the full nested cross-validation and permutation-testing outputs for the FP and FPs problem formulations across AdaBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and XGBoost. It includes observed-label runs, 720 permutation runs, out-of-fold predictions, fold-level results, selected-feature records, ROC data, and run summaries. The raw aero-engine observations are not included in this deposit. The target_index field in the out-of-fold prediction files is an internally generated zero-based positional index used by the outer cross-validation procedure and is not an original dataset identifier. The source code and reproducibility workflow are archived separately on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23348132.

title: Classical capacity of squeezed-noise channels: optimal photon allocation without entangled encoding
abstract: Directional optical noise makes photons pay for both squeezing and signal modulation. This paper determines the optimal transmitter and the ultimate classical communication rate, even when arbitrary entangled and non-Gaussian encodings across many channel uses are allowed. For a finite collection of independent squeezed thermal attenuators with different losses and noise covariances, the complete quantum optimization reduces exactly to a scalar allocation of the total mean photon budget. The result covers every input energy, including the low-energy regime in which only one quadrature should be modulated, channels receiving zero photons, and pure squeezed environments. 1. Exact capacity and all-block additivity. Let \(\Phi=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{d}\Phi_j\), let \(E\ge0\) be the total average input photon number per block, and let \(C_j(E_j)\) be the explicitly attained one-channel rate specified in the paper. Then \[ C(\Phi,E)=\chi_\Phi(E)=\max_{E_j\ge0,\,\sum_jE_j\le E}\sum_{j=1}^{d} C_j(E_j), \] \[ \chi_{\Phi^{\otimes n}}(nE)=nC(\Phi,E)\qquad(n\ge1). \] The optimization includes arbitrary joint input ensembles, with an average physical photon constraint and unrestricted decoding. Independent Gaussian modulation of pure squeezed states attains the answer. Thus neither non-Gaussian codewords nor entanglement across the specified independent channels or repeated blocks improves the capacity. Information quantities use natural logarithms; division by \(\ln2\) gives bits. 2. From measured channel noise to a transmitter design. In quadratures with vacuum covariance \(I/2\), each channel acts as \(V\mapsto\eta V+\operatorname{diag}(y_q,y_p)\), where \(0<\eta<1\), \(y_q\ge y_p>0\), and \(y_qy_p\ge(1-\eta)^2/4\). Define \[ u_e=\frac12\sqrt{\frac{y_q}{y_p}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{th}}=u_e-\frac12+\frac{y_q-y_p}{2\eta}. \] Below this threshold, a bounded one-dimensional maximization determines the optimal seed squeezing and the modulation of the quieter quadrature. Above it, both quadratures can be modulated and the average output is isotropic. Writing \(g(x)=(x+1)\ln(x+1)-x\ln x\), the high-energy rate is \[ C_j(E)=g\!\left(\eta E+\frac{\eta+y_q+y_p-1}{2}\right)-g\!\left(\frac{\eta}{2}+\sqrt{y_qy_p}-\frac12\right),\quad E\ge E_{\mathrm{th}}. \] Both seed squeezing and signal modulation are charged to the same physical input budget. The manuscript gives the low-energy variational formula and the attaining covariances explicitly. 3. When should another channel receive photons? The one-channel capacity curves are increasing and concave. For strictly mixed environments, the optimal allocation equalizes marginal information gains: \[ C_j'(E_j^*)=\lambda\quad(E_j^*>0),\qquad C_j'(0+)\le\lambda\quad(E_j^*=0). \] A previously unused channel turns on when its initial information gain becomes competitive with the declining gain of the channels already in use. Pure-environment endpoints follow by continuity of the attained capacity. In the two-channel example in Figure 1, the second channel activates at total budget approximately \(E=0.436\) photons. The figures evaluate the analytic allocation law and display how photons divide between squeezing, modulation and different links. 4. A converse for the complete correlated input. A joint quadratic output-entropy support excludes all competing encodings. Its proof develops a sharp thermal-reference contraction using both Bogoliubov orientations and independently adjusted thermal references. The appendix supplies the regularized minimizer, Gibbs identity, full-state Hessian comparison, interpolation domains, residual propagation and limiting arguments. This connects a computable Gaussian transmitter design to a bound on every allowed quantum code. Use and scope. Communication theorists and optical-source designers can use measured loss and quadrature noise to allocate a common photon budget, choose the seed squeezing and modulation, identify inactive channels, and calculate an attained capacity benchmark for these memoryless channels. The all-energy result addresses the low-energy Holevo additivity question for a squeezed thermal attenuator, and extends it to heterogeneous finite products under one total budget. Version 1.0, 13 October 2026. The 16-page PDF contains the article, two vector figures, complete supplementary proofs and references.

title: Metadata about AI-generated stories: expert, human annotation relating to conflict, character gender and profession
abstract: This dataset contains 416 human annotations of AI-generated stories. Each row records a story identifier and observations about the story's protagonist, potential opponent, supporting character, and types of conflict, including violent, non-violent, and internal conflict. It also records whether the protagonist responds actively or passively to conflict, along with narrative descriptions and optional annotator notes.

title: Метод аналізу семантичної динаміки діалогів із формуванням пояснення результатів у цифрових сервісах психологічної підтримки
abstract: У статті розглянуто задачу аналізу семантичної динаміки діалогів у цифрових сервісах психологічної підтримки населення.Актуальність дослідження зумовлена тим, що зміст діалогу формується не лише окремими репліками, а й послідовністю станів, тематичних переходів, емоційних змін, комунікативних намірів і контекстних зв'язків між повідомленнями.Метою роботи є розроблення методу аналізу семантичної динаміки діалогів із формуванням пояснення результатів на основі графово-контекстного представлення.Запропонований метод подає діалог як траєкторію смислових станів, побудовану на основі семантичних профілів реплік, типізованих зв'язків графа, локальних фрагментів діалогу та матриці переходів між станами.У межах методу формалізовано показники тематичної та емоційної зміни, узгодженості переходу, подібності траєкторій станів, а також правила виявлення динамічних ситуацій: узгодженого розвитку, зміни теми, повторення станів, відсутності просування та ескалаційного фрагмента.Для інтерпретації результату формується пояснювальний підграф, який містить найбільш значущі репліки, теми, емоційні маркери, комунікативні наміри, стани та зв'язки між ними.Експериментальне дослідження виконано на основі відкритого набору даних MentalChat16K.Із набору було сформовано вибірку з 720 діалогів і 4800 реплік.Порівняння з текстовими та лінійно-контекстними підходами показало, що графово-контекстна модель забезпечує значення TransitionAcc на рівні 0,78 і SeqSim на рівні 0,74.Додавання пояснювального механізму підвищило Fidelity з 0,16 до 0,24 та зменшило Compactness до 0,18.Отримані результати підтверджують доцільність використання запропонованого методу для автоматизованого аналізу розвитку діалогу та формування пояснюваних результатів у цифрових сервісах психологічної підтримки.

title: End-to-End Vision-Language-Action Policies for Autonomous Lunar Rover Docking
abstract: Surface navigation on the Moon is subject to extreme illumination contrast and deployment-time perceptual disturbances. While modular navigation pipelines have long supported planetary rover navigation, robustness is compromised by measurement errors that propagate through hand-engineered components. End-to-end learned policies are an alternative approach to navigation, which maps observations directly to control actions without intermediate components. Vision-language-action models, in particular, have driven significant breakthroughs in robotics and autonomous vehicle research. By leveraging internet-scale vision-language pretraining, these models can be exploited for their commonsense reasoning and visual understanding to provide robust generalization with limited task-specific data. However, their applicability and performance have yet to be characterized for lunar surface operations. In this study, we design a vision-language-action policy for autonomous lunar rover docking and characterize its performance relative to a modular navigation pipeline. We develop a scalable training framework that generates safety-aware expert demonstrations in a high-fidelity lunar simulation environment. In closed-loop evaluations, our policy performs competitively relative to the modular baseline under perceptual disturbances unseen during training. To address the tradeoff between compute consumption and closed-loop safety, the policy adapts its execution horizon by determining how far the rover may safely travel in open loop. Adaptive-horizon execution reduces inference frequency while limiting hazard-contact rates relative to fixed horizons in the evaluated scenarios.

title: Denoise X: Self-Supervised U-Net for Quantum Mottle Suppression in Chest Radiography
abstract: Deep learning for medical image restoration is often constrained by the need for paired training data. Acquiring perfectly registered clean-noisy radiographs in vivo is impractical due to patient motion and radiation-dose limits. To address this, we employ a self-supervised Noise2Noise paradigm that trains on independently corrupted observations without paired clean images. We propose Denoise X, a lightweight self-supervised U-Net model (7.79M parameters) for suppressing quantum mottle and electronic readout noise in low-dose chest radiographs. It is trained on the NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset (112,120 images) using a stochastic Poisson-Gaussian noise simulator. Zero-shot evaluation on the unseen Montgomery County dataset achieved a PSNR of 36.09 dB and SSIM of 0.8806, outperforming the Bilateral filter while preserving high-frequency anatomical details. Using patch-wise inference, Denoise X processes native-resolution chest radiographs in ~2.2 s per image on a Tesla P100 GPU. Cross-domain evaluation on the Shenzhen dataset achieved 36.44 dB PSNR and 0.9099 SSIM, showing strong generalization. For resource-constrained deployment, the model was converted into a 31.16 MB ONNX model for efficient CPU inference on non-DICOM images.

title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction
abstract: The world encompasses both physical environments and human actors. Predicting its evolution requires understanding both physical laws and how emotions shape human actions. However, existing world model benchmarks primarily assess physical plausibility and perceptual quality, leaving emotion-driven world evolution largely untested.We introduce AffectWorld, a benchmark that evaluates the chain Emotion-Action-World State through three tasks: World-State Consistency, Emotion-Action Consistency, and Causal Consistency. It comprises 1,498 everyday video samples annotated with plausible emotions, action tendencies, and atomic world-state constraints. A counterfactual subset of 233 samples tests whether changing an agent's emotion under fixed scene and event conditions yields corresponding changes in actions and consequences. We define eight metrics across the three tasks and an additional counterfactual metric, combining automatic visual assessment with human-calibrated VLM/LLM judgments. Evaluations of five SoTA world models (e.g., Cosmos3) required world-state change scores of 0.100-0.280 and counterfactual emotion sensitivity scores of 0.027-0.070 on a [0, 1] scale. These results reveal substantial gaps in generating the consequences of emotion-driven actions and adapting future predictions to emotional interventions. AffectWorld provides a testbed for advancing world models that capture how emotions shape future physical and social states.

title: Beyond Black Boxes: Visual Grounding for Text Embeddings
abstract: In this paper, our goal is to represent text embeddings as sketches for three main reasons. First, to visualize text representation and to explore their potential their potential for AI explainability. Second, to investigate the potential benefits of the sketch-based representation for information retrieval. Third, to explore their potential for reasoning, drawing inspiration from the concept of mental imagery. We propose a sketch-based visual grounding framework that transforms text representations into visual topographic sketches. Our approach aims to emphasis the semantics content encoded in the text embeddings through the corresponding sketch. Evaluations are conducted on the MS-COCO dataset to examine the utility of these sketches for text retrieval. The comparative study of SBERT and Sketch-based method reveals that SBERT retains an advantage in strict top-1 retrieval accuracy while achieving comparable performance to the sketch-based method in top-5 retrieval. A cascaded approach combining SBERT and the sketch-based method outperforms SBERT alone, suggesting that the Sketch-based representation could offer significant potential for information retrieval if trained directly on text.

title: Multimodal Fusion of RGB and Complementary Modalities for Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation adds an auxiliary sensing stream to RGB images (RGB-X), such as thermal, LiDAR, depth, event, polarization, or light field. This can improve robustness in poor lighting and under motion blur. But different sensors often produce features that do not match well, and fusion can become unstable. To alleviate these issues, we propose a bidirectional polarity-aware cross-modality fusion (BPCF) module that effectively captures complementary cues while enhancing feature alignment. We evaluate the framework on six modality pairings: RGB-Thermal, RGB-LiDAR, RGB-Depth, RGB-Event, RGB-Polarization, and RGB-Light Field. Our model achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on eight public datasets, including MFNet, KITTI-360, DELIVER, DDD17, DSEC, MCubeS, ZJU, and UrbanLF. The codes and trained models will be released upon acceptance.

title: Arithmetic by Machine Learning: Learning the Four Arithmetic Operations, Exponentiation and Logarithm with Small Perceptrons
abstract: We study whether the four basic arithmetic operations, exponentiation a^b and the logarithm log_a b can be realised by small perceptrons trained by gradient descent. For each operation a small network is designed so that an exact solution exists in its weight space. For the four arithmetic operations and the logarithm, we test whether training from random initial weights on input–output examples finds this solution; for exponentiation, we verify the exact representation and the numerical convergence of training guided toward the known weights.Addition and subtraction are learned by a single linear layer. Multiplication uses a hidden layer with square activation and converges to the polarization identity ab = ¼[(a+b)² − (a−b)²]. Division uses a logarithmic hidden layer and an exponential output with complex-valued forward computation. The logarithm uses a log-log hidden layer and converges to the exact solution with Adam. Exponentiation uses a sign-dependent log-type activation and a double-exponential output, representing a^b exactly for a, b > e; it reaches the exact weights only with an auxiliary loss toward them, so learning it from examples alone remains open.This report consolidates the author's own series of Qiita articles (2018–2026). The square-activation multiplication network (2018) and the complex-valued division network (January 2020) were developed independently of, and published before, Neural Arithmetic Logic Units (2018) and Neural Power Units (2020), respectively.

title: RIDI-PREDICT-v1: generation archive and post-run analysis recovery (Supplementary Data 4)
abstract: Supplementary Data 4 for the RIDI study, “Identical evaluation scores conceal which questions language models answer correctly”. This archive contains the RIDI-PREDICT-v1 frozen study materials, per-question generation records for all 24 planned model-by-benchmark-by-draw units, original failed analysis and diagnostic records, and the dated post-run analysis-recovery amendment, derivative script, results and verification receipts. The registered Qwen3-32B logistic model did not converge because of quasi-complete separation. Qwen H3a and its regression-dependent S3 remain unavailable; unaffected analyses completed under the disclosed recovery amendment. No human-annotation results are included.
