title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration–exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism, employees’ AI use modes, leader temporal myopia, and employee radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery. We distinguish leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism into perceived technological dynamism and perceived market dynamism, and employees’ AI use into exploratory and exploitative AI use. The model is tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling and three-wave matched survey data from 368 leader–employee dyads. The results show that leader-perceived technological dynamism is positively associated with employee exploratory AI use, whereas leader-perceived market dynamism is positively associated with employee exploitative AI use. Exploratory AI use is positively associated with employee radical creativity, whereas exploitative AI use is negatively associated with it. Leader temporal myopia weakens the positive conditional indirect relationship of technological dynamism with radical creativity through exploratory AI use and strengthens the negative conditional indirect relationship of market dynamism with radical creativity through exploitative AI use. By adopting a knowledge-activity perspective, this study reveals the differentiated relationships between AI use modes and radical creativity and further explains how perceptions of the external environment, leaders’ temporal orientation, and employees’ AI use behaviors are differentially related. The findings provide a theoretical basis and practical implications for helping firms engaged in AI-enabled drug discovery guide employees toward effective AI use and enhance radical creativity.

title: A multidimensional knowledge tracing hybrid model integrating semantics and dialogue behavior for cultural education
abstract: In intelligent dialogue systems for cultural teaching, traditional knowledge tracing models exhibit a limited capacity to interpret open-ended responses and struggle to characterize multidimensional cultural learning abilities or to effectively leverage the structural information embedded in instructional dialogues. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SAINT+ (Separated Self-Attentive Neural Knowledge Tracing)–DKVMN (Dynamic Key-Value Memory Network) hybrid knowledge tracing model tailored for cultural teaching. The core idea is to introduce semantic–dialogue–ability structural constraints at both the sequence modeling and memory modeling levels simultaneously. Specifically, the model unifies the semantic information of students' open-ended responses—encoded via RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach)—with dialogue-behavior features into structured learning events, thereby incorporating the dialogue process into sequence modeling. At the memory layer, the conventional single-dimensional mastery probability is extended into multidimensional concept mastery states, capturing the evolution of distinct ability dimensions in cultural learning, including factual understanding, explanatory ability, reflective depth, and confidence. The traceability of state transitions is further enhanced through an update mechanism constrained by behavioral conditions. Building on these components, the model achieves a balance between predictive performance and interpretability through joint multi-task training. Experimental results show that the proposed model attains an overall prediction accuracy of 0.862 (95% CI 0.856, 0.868) and an AUC (Area Under the Curve) of 0.905 (95% CI 0.899, 0.912). For the rubric classification of open-ended responses, the overall accuracy reaches approximately 0.877, with RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) values ranging from 0.09 to 0.11 across all ability dimensions. Moreover, the designed attention and memory-writing visualizations provide teachers with traceable concept-level evidence of student learning. Overall, the experiments demonstrate that the proposed model offers strong effectiveness and interpretability in intelligent dialogue systems for cultural teaching, providing reliable technical support for intelligent tutoring systems aimed at cultivating complex cultural competencies.

title: Designing for Prediction: Planning Formulas for Expected Out-of-Sample $R^2$ and $r$
abstract: Design calculations let researchers gauge, before data is collected, whether a planned study is likely to detect an effect. In this paper, we develop such calculations for predictive models using ordinary least squares and ridge regression under leave-one-out cross-validation. To do so, we derive closed-form expressions relating the expected out-of-sample $R^2$ and the expected correlation between observed and predicted outcomes to four design-stage quantities: sample size, number of predictors, an assumed population $R^2$ ($ρ^2_{in}$) and a design efficiency factor $D^*$ (which summarizes how leverage is distributed across observations). Unlike the classical shrinkage formulas, which depend only on sample size and dimension, these are sensitive to how covariates are arranged -- to imbalance and skew. A simulation study assesses the accuracy of the formulas against realized values under a variety of data generating mechanisms. We apply the methods to a published study predicting personality from smartphone behavior and show that the design formulas would have indicated, before any analyses were run, that least squares could not be expected to beat the sample mean while ridge could. An R package, predpower, implements the calculations.

title: OpenMQPI: An MLIR-based Pipeline to Offload Quantum Circuits via OpenMP
abstract: Quantum computing introduces specialized software stacks and programming interfaces that are often tightly coupled to specific ecosystems and hardware backends, limiting interoperability and software reuse. For HPCQC application developers, this complicates the integration of quantum accelerators into existing applications. Existing quantum frameworks also use ecosystem-specific circuit representations and compilation pipelines, hindering integration with established heterogeneous compiler infrastructures. We propose OpenMQPI, an MLIR-based OpenMP extension for quantum programming that leverages OpenMP's standardized target offloading infrastructure to integrate quantum resources into HPC applications. OpenMQPI introduces QPIR, a lightweight MLIR dialect for representing quantum circuits within OpenMP target regions, and a compiler pipeline that performs quantum-specific optimizations and lowers circuits to executables compatible with OpenMP offloading. At runtime, an MQSS plugin enables the generated executable to offload quantum circuits to quantum hardware through the OpenMP target offloading model. We evaluate OpenMQPI using the VQE, QFT, and Deutsch-Jozsa algorithms with 5, 10, 15, and 20 qubits, comparing execution times against Qiskit and CUDA Quantum. OpenMQPI achieves the lowest average VQE execution time across all tested qubit configurations. At 20 qubits, it requires 5.18 s, compared with 5.83 s for Qiskit and 7.39 s for CUDA Quantum. For QFT and Deutsch-Jozsa, OpenMQPI achieves execution times comparable to Qiskit and lower than those of CUDA Quantum.

title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics
abstract: High-fidelity three-dimensional turbulent flow fields are essential for scientific and engineering analyses, yet obtaining them through direct numerical simulation or high-resolution measurements remains expensive. Super-resolution reconstruction from coarse-grained data therefore offers a promising alternative, but remains fundamentally challenging because fine-scale structures are intrinsically three-dimensional and dynamically coupled across scales. Existing data-driven approaches still struggle to recover multiscale volumetric structures and their coherent temporal evolution. To address these limitations, we propose a turbulence-aware framework for time-resolved three-dimensional flow reconstruction. The framework couples a multiscale neural operator, designed to recover volumetric structures, with a state space model to promote temporal consistency in the reconstructed dynamics. In addition, Navier-Stokes residuals are incorporated as soft constraints to regularize the reconstruction toward physically plausible dynamics. A mixture-of-experts mechanism is also introduced to support unsupervised adaptation to unknown coarse-graining. Across evaluations on canonical turbulent systems and atmospheric reanalysis data, the proposed framework reduces reconstruction errors relative to learning-based and classical baselines, while better preserving multiscale spatial structure and coherent temporal evolution. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in reconstructing high-fidelity three-dimensional flow fields from coarse-grained data.

title: PLEDGE: Progressive Lossy Error-Bounded Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) codecs report reconstruction quality after compression, and give users little control over the distortion of individual primitives. We present PLEDGE, a training-free, progressive, error-bounded codec that translates four user-declared tolerances into per-primitive quantization bounds: screen-space position, footprint deformation due to rotation and scale, view-dependent color, and opacity. The bounds apply throughout a declared camera domain, including previously unseen viewpoints. Position and opacity are bounded directly; footprint deformation is bounded under the rasterizer's affine projection model, and color is bounded over all viewing directions. PLEDGE organizes quantized residuals into a progressive bitstream with explicit error bounds for every valid prefix. Experiments across thirteen scenes verify all declared per-mechanism bounds and demonstrate competitive rate-distortion performance. The four tolerances incur substantially different rate costs, so users can spend rate where their application needs it.

title: Artifact for Analyzing Unbounded Probabilistic Loops using Characteristic Function Recurrences
abstract: Artifact for the paper "Analyzing Unbounded Probabilistic Loops using Characteristic Function Recurrences", conditionally accepted at POPL 2027.The artifact is a VirtualBox virtual machine image (about 4.9 GB), downloadable as a .ova file (Artifact-VM.ova). It needs VirtualBox 7.1 or later. The guest is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Desktop (x86-64), pre-configured with 8 GB RAM and 4 CPUs. No network access is needed inside the VM.The virtual machine was built and tested with VirtualBox 7.2.20 on Windows 11 Pro (x86-64), on an Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX laptop (24 cores, 32 GB RAM). We recommend that the artifact is run on hosts having at least 16 GB RAM. The artifact has not been tested on macOS, on Apple-silicon (ARM) hosts: since the image is x86-64 so we expect it to run slowly under emulation.For further information and instruction on how to run the artifact see README.md (also available in the VM at /home/artifact/Artifact/README.md).

title: Joint Refinement of Center of Gravity Thresholds for Color Quantization: Code and Per-Image Results
abstract: Source code and full-precision per-image results for the article "Joint Refinement of Center of Gravity Thresholds for Color Quantization: Gains and Limits of Separable Color Partitions", submitted to Computer Vision and Image Understanding. The deposit contains the C# implementation of the proposed methods (CoG+BRO and CoG+CD) and the CvqBench benchmark, the Python baselines, the exact block coordinate descent, the analysis, statistics and figure scripts, the pre-specified analysis plans, the random seeds, and the per-image results underlying all tables. Third-party image datasets are not redistributed; image identifiers and sources are listed in IMAGE_LISTS.md, and README.md explains how to rebuild and reproduce the results.

evidence.title: Joint Refinement of Center of Gravity Thresholds for Color Quantization: Code and Per-Image Results
evidence.abstract: Source code and full-precision per-image results for the article "Joint Refinement of Center of Gravity Thresholds for Color Quantization: Gains and Limits of Separable Color Partitions", submitted to Computer Vision and Image Understanding. The deposit contains the C# implementation of the proposed methods (CoG+BRO and CoG+CD) and the CvqBench benchmark, the Python baselines, the exact block coordinate descent, the analysis, statistics and figure scripts, the pre-specified analysis plans, the random seeds, and the per-image results underlying all tables. Third-party image datasets are not redistributed; image identifiers and sources are listed in IMAGE_LISTS.md, and README.md explains how to rebuild and reproduce the results.

title: Jethro Hierarchical Multi-Agent Orchestration: A Scalable 10-50-100-1000 Delegation Control Plane with Hard Scoped Budgets for Autonomous Enterprises
abstract: As enterprises transition from single-turn Large Language Model (LLM) assistants to large-scale multi-agent swarms, flat peer-to-peer and centralized star topologies suffer from severe coordination bottlenecks, exponential O(N^2) communication overhead, context window degradation, and unconstrained API token expenditure. Drawing inspiration from the classical Jethro organizational principle of tiered delegation (groups of 10, 50, 100, and 1000), this paper introduces the Jethro Hierarchical Multi-Agent Orchestration (JHMO) architecture. JHMO establishes a deterministic 4-tier enterprise control plane comprising: (1) Tier-10 Tactical Execution Squads, (2) Tier-50 Domain Supervisors (Maker-Checker verification gates), (3) Tier-100 Departmental Orchestrators, and (4) Tier-1000 Executive Control Plane with hard scoped budget circuit breakers and Human-in-the-Loop board gating. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate a 98.1% reduction in redundant context tokens and 99.6% task completion fidelity.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Kazakh-Language Educational Assistants: Sentiment Classification and Question Answering with and Without Context
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in education, but evidence on their performance comes mainly from high-resource languages. We evaluated five commercial LLMs in Kazakh in a zero-shot setting: sentiment classification on 300 class-balanced KazSAnDRA reviews and question answering (QA) on the same 300 randomly sampled KazQAD questions with and without the gold supporting passage. Exact McNemar tests with Holm correction found no significant pairwise differences on sentiment classification, one with supporting context, and nine without context under the Containment criterion. For OpenAI and Anthropic, the higher-tier model had a larger advantage over its lower-tier counterpart when the supporting passage was removed (tier-by-regime interaction: OR = 1.92, 95% CI [1.52, 2.43]). Closed-book scores were affected by output format, inflectional morphology, and answer length. Human evaluation of 500 QA responses showed that string-based metrics substantially underestimated closed-book accuracy (0.55 by human judgement versus 0.26 by Containment). Under human judgement, the three higher-scoring models did not differ significantly from one another. Access to a relevant passage narrowed differences between models, although this oracle-context condition did not test a retrieval system. These findings support task-specific evaluation of Kazakh-language educational assistants and the use of answer-matching criteria checked against human judgement.

title: Annotated Food Recipe Dataset for Allergen Identification Using Natural Language Processing Techniques
abstract: This dataset contains annotated Indonesian recipe texts for allergen identification and Named Entity Recognition (NER) tasks. The dataset was constructed from Indonesian food recipes and consists of token-level annotations containing word sequences, Part-of-Speech (POS) tags, and allergen entity labels. Each sentence in the dataset is segmented into individual tokens and annotated using the BIO tagging scheme to identify allergen-related entities. The dataset provides linguistic information through POS tagging, which can be utilized as additional features for natural language processing models, particularly for allergen detection, information extraction, and NER-based applications in the culinary domain. The dataset contains 24,000 annotated tokens extracted from Indonesian recipes. Each record includes four attributes: 1. Recipe #: Identifier of the recipe source. 2. Word: Individual token or word extracted from the recipe text. 3. POS: Part-of-Speech category assigned to each token. 4. Tag: BIO annotation label representing allergen-related entities. This dataset supports research in Indonesian Natural Language Processing (NLP), especially for developing and evaluating machine learning and deep learning models for food allergen recognition.

title: When AI ads violate expectations: the interplay of AI character, product type, and advertising appeal of AI ads on consumer attitudes
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping video advertising production. Using expectancy violations theory as an interpretive lens, this study develops a framework in which ad appeal (rational vs. emotional), product type (high-tech vs. low-tech), and AI character embodiment (no character vs. animal-like vs. human-like) jointly relate to ad attitude and to two appraisals: perceived novelty and perceived uncanniness. This study tests the framework in five between-subjects experiments with consumers recruited from an online panel. Results show that rational appeals outperform emotional appeals in AI-generated ads, especially for low-tech products. Novelty is positively and uncanniness negatively associated with ad attitude, and the indirect effects through both appraisals are consistent with the proposed process. Human-like AI characters amplify uncanniness in emotional low-tech executions. In one rational low-tech execution, an animal-like character lowered uncanniness relative to a no-character baseline, but ad attitude did not differ significantly. The findings extend expectancy-violation theorizing in AI advertising and offer configuration-level design guidance for brands deploying disclosed AI-generated advertising.
